A declared repository's `visibility` (`company`, unset, or `unit`; `CodeVisibilities`, held to the domain's own set both ways by an engine test) is which SEATS read it, and warns, never refuses, where a `unit` repository's owning unit has no effective lead; its `search` (`indexed`, unset, or `grep`; `CodeSearchModes`, held to the domain's own set both ways by an engine test) is how code search reads it, unset `indexed` by `CodeSearchMode.Resolved`, the one place — a project the company declares is the code a search across its repositories reads, while a repository a tool makes starts at `grep`, the code domain's; `code.limits` holds three SIZES that nest — a file inside a push inside a repository, ordered on what a push is held to with the defaults resolved (`CodeLimits.Resolved`, the one place) and refused at the field the document sets — and a seat's daily COUNT, `pushes_per_seat_day` (1..100 000, unset 1 000), which no order rule reads and which bounds what a seat pushing in a loop costs the code log rather than budgeting its work; `code.identity_domain` is the domain an engine-built commit spells its addresses in — its committer's `engine@<domain>` and a seat's `<handle>@<domain>` where its role states no address — a lowercase DNS name of at most `CodeMaxIdentityDomainBytes` (189: the 254 an address may be less the `@` and `iam.MaxLogin`'s 64-byte handle, so every address spelled in it is one a mail system takes), unset `seats.invalid` under RFC 2606's reserved `.invalid` (`IdentityDomainResolved`, the one place the default is applied), and refused without `code.backend: gitlet` like the rest of the block; a seat's `code.access` warns that it grants nothing on a company with no `code.backend: gitlet`. A seat's code tier is ONE FIELD, `role.code.access` — Gitlet's cap on what the chart grants, owned here as its three constants (`TierReadOnly`, `TierReview`, `TierFullAccess`), which `internal/code` reads — and no vendor's: a GitHub seat's reach is its app's `role.github.permissions`, which a tier no longer mints. It takes exactly its three tiers, `read_only`, `review` and `full_access`, each in one spelling, folding no hyphen, case or space — no tag shipped the field, so a second spelling would be a compatibility path for a version that never existed, and the schema lists the three as its enum and must refuse nothing the engine runs; and a human seat carrying it is refused by an ADMISSION rule, since a person acts as their own identity on every host and nothing running reads a tier off a human seat. THE KEYRING IS REQUIRED ON EVERY NODE, serving or not, a node without `data` included (`secrets.keys`, `validateTopology`): every state-log record a data node applies is signed and verified under it, every request a node without data sends a data node's estate service is signed under it (ADR-0031), the company document a node fetches from its peers is authenticated by its seal, and a node serving the API signs every session cookie with it, so `Secrets.Cipher` refuses an empty keyring rather than handing back the nil that used to mean plaintext. AND SO IS A STREAM THAT SURVIVES A RESTART on every broker MEMBER (`stream.store_dir` on an embedded member, a single node included, `Stream.Durable`, asked by `Validate` and again at `engine.New`'s door before anything opens), while a leaf, a node without `data`, which keeps no stream, is REFUSED one: every data node keeps its state logs on the stream from boot, company or none, so an in-memory member is a node whose first restart leaves it unable to serve. It was a CROSS-TIER rule (`CheckTiers`, deleted with it) asked only of a company, which let through exactly the node started with none, and no rule needs both documents any more. THREE MORE SETTINGS STOP BEING OPTIONAL the moment a node SERVES THE API (`Bootstrap.ServesAPI`: `api.port` non-zero AND the `ingress` role, on the Bootstrap rather than the API block because half the answer is the node block's roles, and a probe-only port needs none of them), and `api.go` is where the rule lives: `api.external_url` (the cookie's Secure flag and __Host- prefix, the origin a write and a socket handshake are judged against, and every link a person follows, the engine is behind a TLS-terminating proxy and can read none of it off the request; it is the vendors' address too unless `api.public` opens a listener for them, whose own `api.public.external_url` is then REQUIRED and is what `API.WebhookBase` answers, so Tier B carries no address at all), `api.auth.admin` (`iam.AdminPosture`: whether THIS node serves `admin`, `serve`, or `refuse`, which clamps admin away and keeps every app, the apps expanded before the clamp, applied per node per request so a mixed fleet is a LEGAL state each node publishes its posture for; the zero is refused naming the field, and an unknown name in a Tier A token's `grants` is refused naming the three, as is `admin` on a `refuse` node) and at least one `api.auth.tokens` entry (a fresh estate is empty, so its session is what creates the company and invites the first person onto a human seat it declares, and the way back in when an administrator has locked themselves out). A token's value is checked on what the `${VAR}` RESOLVES to, which is the only place the floor bites, and `api.trusted_proxies` is a CIDR list and never a bool, because the question is whether THIS peer is the proxy. `api.auth.company_writers` names the Tier A tokens that alone may change a MANAGED company document (ADR-0030), each entry held to the token-id grammar and judged on the CREDENTIAL a write came through (`MayWriteCompany`, which the viewer answer reads too), so a person's session, a machine token and a lead's subtree write are all refused while it is set. `allow_anonymous_read` and `api.auth.disabled` are DELETED, and a file still carrying either is refused at its line like any unknown key (`KnownFields`, so no retired posture can be silently inverted when the key itself is refused) but BY NAME, through `removedKeys` (`removed.go`), which says the key was removed and what replaces it, because the generic refusal tells somebody upgrading an old file to check a spelling no spelling passes, keyed on the block's Go type, since `disabled:` anywhere but `api.auth` is an ordinary typo and reads like one: the first was a bool whose safe value was its zero and which was `omitempty`, so closing it did not survive an export round trip, and the second authenticated the EMPTY credential into full operator authority, and so is `api.auth.oidc`, because nobody signs in through a third party any more, and with it went the BACKEND SELECTOR: password sign-in is always served, since a deployment nobody was invited to already signs nobody in, and `api.auth.totp` (UNSET IS `required`, so `optional` is always somebody's explicit choice), `accept_insecure` and `min_password_length` sit directly under `api.auth`; and so is `api.auth.bootstrap`, because the Tier A token IS the credential a company has before it has anybody, so the first person is invited under it like everybody after them, onto a human seat. `DiffOrg` is what a `/config` write CHANGES in Tier B, object by object: every seat (by handle) and unit (by key) added, removed, moved or edited, each with the PLACES it reaches, where it was and is, a unit itself when its own fields change, what a NEW `lead:` or `manages:` entry names, every object whose `lead:` or `manages:` entry already states the id an ADDED seat or unit takes (a dangling `lead: ghost` is taken over by adding `ghost` anywhere), plus the KEYS another system finds a seat or unit by that it sets, clears or alters (a project, space, channel, email or contact identity, all `admin`'s: a project outlives the unit that declared it and an account exists at its vendor, so who else holds a key is not a fact two documents state, and judged against the document's own objects a lead declared an orphaned project their team's and became its lead), the credentials it touches, each credential field compared WHOLE, keys included (a key of an `mcp_env` block is laid over its server's own value for the seat's child, an empty one included, and a walk of the strings alone found nothing in it), with every `${VAR}` it touches in ANY field counted among them (a seat's `email` and contact ids resolve a whole reference through the secret store and the engine's own environment, and are recited to whoever looks the seat up), and the settings keys that differ, because the org chart's leads may write their own subtree and each of those places is a subtree decision (internal/authz's). The GRANTS a seat's role carries that it sets or clears (`OrgChange.Grants`, today `health_tools`) are listed apart and are `admin`'s too: a grant opens what only an administrator reads, so a lead who could set one in their own subtree would read it through their seat. A human seat carrying `health_tools` is refused at admission (`validateHumanSeatGrants`): the grant decides only an agent, and a person reads those tools as an administrator. Only what the write changes is judged, and two objects on one id are placed at the root, nobody's subtree. THE EXECUTOR RULES ARE THE WHOLE DOCUMENT'S (`company.go`, `budget.go`), each RUNNABLE because no turn of the seat it names could run: a company with an agent seat and a `providers.llm` entry needs `providers.sandbox`, one refusal at the block naming the first such seat (`validateSandboxPlacement`; a company with no model yet is an org chart written before its credentials and needs none), and every runner-capable member of every agent seat's executor chain has to resolve a cell the catalogue configures; a seat whose executor chain holds no `claude-code` or `opencode` member is refused at its `llm`, or once at the `agent` of the entry seats with none fall to (`validateExecutors`), while a chain that mixes one with another harness is a warning (`executorWarnings`), since the other harness still serves the seat's reviewer, workers and side passes; `run_in` on a harness with no in-box runner is refused as a placement nothing reads (`LLMProvider.validate`); and a `token_budget` ceiling below `turn_engine.executor_min_budget_tokens` is refused at the ceiling (`validateExecutorFloor`), because such a seat parks as starved before its first launch and stays parked; a `providers.llm` key matches `ProviderKeyPattern` (a DNS label with dots and underscores) and no two keys share a credential bundle variable, refused on a write and warned on apply, since two such keys silently shared one login; and `ProviderReferences` is the ONE walk of every field that names an entry (a seat's `llm` as a scalar, list or mapping, its flat per-phase fields, `assistant.llm` and `assistant.deep_work`), each with the segments of the written field, which `validateProviderKeys` reads too; `MCPServerReferences` is the same for an MCP server (every seat's and unit's `mcp_env` block keyed on it and every `sandbox.mcp.servers` entry, a block the engine reads by its own name marked `EngineRead`), which the admission rule refusing a field that names no declared server (`validateMCPServerReferences`) and a server's removal (`RemoveMCPServer`) both read; `MCPValueSlot`, `PointMCPValue` and `MCPValueKeys` (mcpvalues.go) place, point and list a server's stored values, and `PointUnwrittenClientSecret` points a service identity's secret its entry leaves out at the variable the values route stores it under, so an entry written through the API never derives one; `MCPServer.Reach` (mcpaccess.go, ADR-0076) is the ONE GRANT, a server's `access` (absent, every agent seat; a unit reaching every agent seat beneath it) or, for a server reading each agent's own vendor credential, the integration lane, which `Grants` adds `enabled` to, and `validateMCPAccess` refuses an `mcp_env` block, a unit's block or a box listing for a server that does not reach its seat, `access` on a vendor-bound server and a grant naming what the chart does not hold, since an `mcp_env` block holds values and grants nothing. EACH TOOL OF A SERVER AT A LEVEL (`mcptools.go`): `tools {default, levels}`, `allow` or `blocked`, keyed by the server's own tool name, decided by `MCPToolPolicy.Level`; `validateBoxToolLevels` refuses an executor box listing of a server any tool of which is held back, since a box dials a server whole, past the engine. A LEAD NARROWS, NEVER WIDENS (`mcplimits.go`): `Grants` reads a limit that turns a server off for the seat (a limit is not a grant, so `Reach` does not), `validateMCPLimits` refuses a limit that holds nothing back, turns a server on, says `allow` or keys no tool, and a box listing of a server a seat's limits hold a tool of back, and `DiffOrg` lists apart every limit a write lifts or loosens for an agent seat both documents hold (`OrgDiff.Widened`), compared as each seat is held so a move out from under a unit's limits counts. `code.scratch` bounds a seat's own SCRATCH repositories, which only its tools create: `idle_days` (7 unless set, 1 to 365 — the floor is a day because a turn holding a repository idle for 22 hours records its hold, `code.HoldRecordAfter`, and the record must land inside the idle window a pass in flight read, which internal/objstore/references holds) and `max_per_seat` (a pointer: unset is 50, 0 allows none, 1000 at most); it is refused without `code.backend: gitlet`. A declared repository's name is a PROJECT's (`gitref.ValidProjectName`), since a dotted name is a seat's scratch repository, and `CodeMaxRepos`, the admission bound on `code.repos`, is also the runtime cap a tool's project create meets (`repo_limit`, declared and tool-made projects counted alike). |
| `configplane` | The control plane: how a fleet agrees which company configuration it is running, and what a node does when it does not have the current one. An append-only ACTIVATION POINTER names the epoch and every node writes its own apply status; a node reads both and picks a posture. Append-only because re-activating an UNCHANGED revision is the credential-rotation gesture, and a pointer keyed on revision id would rebuild nothing on exactly that operation. Lag alone never sheds: it must be CONFIRMED — a failed attempt of the node's own, or behind past `LagGrace` — and `FleetView.LagConfirmed` is that rule stated once, which the posture and the engine's irreversible judgements (the mailbox retirement, the code purge) both read, so a node the posture reads as waiting is never one another reader warns is behind. THE POINTER IS THE COMPANY (ADR-0057, in the package doc's "Three facts about a company's configuration"): every config read and the base of every config write answer it whenever there is one, on every node alike, never a node's own row, and a node keeps three facts of its own about it, each with one writer — what it BOOTS on, moved online only to a revision its engine has applied; the FLEET's revision as it last saw it, refused or not, which is what it restores when the pointer is gone; and an offline OFFER, published only by a compare-and-set over the base it was built on. One flag for all three made a node boot on a revision it had refused, walked a write back, and published an offline change over a fleet that had moved on. `RevisionOf` is the ONE mapping from the pointer and the body it carries to a history row, for the reconciler, the config API and the boot alike, at the pointer's instant and under the origin's record, because each reader built its own and they disagreed on whose record a revision was — and it is why this package imports `coord` and `store` |
| `seat` | Which seats this node runs. The placement policy is deliberately dumb — greedy claim to `ceil(seats / live nodes)`, converging in BOTH directions, `preferred` orders the attempt and never gates it; a change to the seat set — an apply adding or removing a role — asks for a pass at once (`Resweep`) rather than leaving every new seat unclaimed until the tick, and so does the CLAIM GATE OPENING (`Config.Ready`), which the host cannot see and the engine asks for — and an asked pass the gate withheld, which claimed and gave back nothing, spends nothing of the one early pass an interval honours, or the ask that says the gate has opened waited for the tick behind an apply's that found the node still catching up. `Host.Start`'s first pass is the only synchronous claim, and on a boot behind its logs it claims nothing; it runs with the HEARTBEAT ALREADY TURNING, because the pass runs each claimed seat's acquire hook inline and a hook can outlast a TTL — started after it, the heartbeat renewed nothing on the boot, so a slow hook lapsed the lease it was building on and the watchdog read the pass as the heartbeat wedged. A RENEW IS SENT A BEAT INSIDE THE HEARTBEAT, on a ticker of its own (`renewPeriod`): `MayStart` admits within a heartbeat of a renew's SENT instant, recorded only once the store answers, so a pass every heartbeat refused a healthy node's seat for every renew's round trip at the shipped TTL, and one counted in received beats slipped by every beat a long pass dropped. A RENEW'S AGE IS THE LARGER OF ITS TWO CLOCK READINGS (`elapsed`), for `MayStart`, `Provable`, `HoldsPresence` and the heartbeat's grace alike: the monotonic reading stops while the host sleeps while the store's TTL runs on, so measured on it alone a node that slept past its TTL woke still proving every lease, and the wall reading alone would let a step back make a renew look younger. A STOP'S COORDINATION STEPS DRAW ON ONE ALLOWANCE (`StopBudget`, one heartbeat interval of the lease TTL, carried on the context and charged only while a step is in flight), so a member that lost its store spends one allowance stopping rather than a bound per step; a layer where a stop may begin takes it with `WithinStop`. `watchdog` is the other half: a wedged event loop cannot be signalled, so the thread's only honest move is to exit — and it is the engine's ONE unilateral exit, so a node whose embedded broker declares itself dead after its boot (nats-server's Fatalf, carried as `jetstream.Death`) leaves through it too (`Watchdog.Fail`), at once and armed or not, because every step a drain would take rides the broker that died — with its OWN exit code (69, `EX_UNAVAILABLE`, beside the wedge's 75), because a restart log is often all a deployment keeps and the two send a reader to opposite places. The heartbeat stamps its beat as it asks each renew, never only once a pass is done, because a renew the store leaves unanswered is held to its read's whole bound and a pass over many seats on a node that cannot reach its store is TURNING — keeping each seat to its own lease's TTL, then dropping it — where a beat stamped once a pass read that as a wedge once the bounds summed past the TTL. The unmanned-role check asks `RoleNeeded` first: `gitlet` is needed only where the company sets `code.backend: gitlet`, and a role that stops being needed while nobody held it is `fleet_role_unneeded`, never `fleet_role_manned`. The PRESENCE ROW each beat writes (`presenceMeta`) is the profile, the host's own counts (`seats_held`, `seats_withdrawn`) and, on a Gitlet node, what its git cache gives its background work (`Config.GitBackground`, `coord.GitBackgroundKey`) — each from memory and written on every beat, the budget's zero included — and the STATUS, from a hook bounded to `StatusBudgetRatio` of the beat and published whole or not at all; a placement input never rides the status, because a beat that gives up on the hook drops it whole, and every peer would read that node as not saying |
| `estate` | The replicated estate ROUTED, from every node — ADR-0025 and its amendment. ONE `Router` runs on EVERY node, with or without `data`, and every seam the tools, the operator's surfaces (the API's tracker, knowledge-base, artifacts and chat routes, the operator's MCP) and the duties consume is answered through it, so a tool cannot tell which kind of node it is on. Every data node holds the whole estate, so the router answers in-process where THIS node's copy serves — held to this node's floors exactly as a remote data node is — and otherwise asks the data nodes its `Placement` names (every live data node, off the WATCHED presence view): the one that answered last first, then the `rendezvous` order on its own id, a node gone silent last for thirty seconds, over that serving node's OWN subjects rather than a scatter or a queue group, because the asker must know which node an unanswered write went to — one for every operation but a push's proposal, which a node answers on a LANE of its own (`crewlet.estate.<node>.proposals`, `proposalAnswers` 3 136 wide: the SUM of what the committer and its two sibling writers each hold node-wide — `code.CommitterNodeProposals` 1 088, `code.ChangeWriterNodeWrites` and `code.ChecksWriterNodeWrites` 1 024 each — every one refusing busy at once past its own share, so no component's burst holds a slot another's requests need), because a proposal holds its answer slot while it waits for its batch, and on the shared registration sixty-four queued pushes held every slot the node answered its reads, its other writes and a git fetch's resolve through; a lane answers only the operations declared on it (`op.answeredOn`) and refuses any other unserved, and a node registers every lane or none. A copy that is WRONG is OUT OF SERVICE — a peer asking is told `out_of_service`, and its node keeps its seats while their calls go to peers — and a copy that LAGS its logs is a worse node to ask, never no node: asked last, and told to answer anyway — and so is a node confirmed BEHIND THE COMPANY'S CONFIGURATION (shed or stuck, never lag alone: `Backend.Current`, the engine's `admits`, the reconciler's `Admits`), on every operation but admission's ungated ping, because what it supplies from its own epoch — the chart a people field and a lead resolve by, a unit, a search's scope, the code limits — is the revision the fleet replaced, a value every reader meets anyway when a revision changes one, while a refusal would cost a fleet whose only data node failed an apply its tracker, pages and usage; it answers a reason of its own, `behind_config`, which an asker REMEMBERS for `suspectFor` (per node, never per copy: the posture is the node's) and meanwhile skips the node for — asking it only as the last resort, after every copy that only lags (whose answer holds the current configuration, in that order whether or not the asker has heard the refusal yet, so every asker sends a repository's pushes to one node), told at once to answer anyway, and a push's runner-up instead — because unlike a lag it LASTS (until the apply succeeds, a stuck node's until a person acts), and forgotten between requests it cost every request one refusal per such node and every push to a repository it commits for its whole proposal; `engine.TestEveryEpochSeamAServingDecideReadsIsClassified` holds every seam a serving decide reads (`worklet.WriterDeps`, `Backend`, `ServerSeams`, the code committer's, change writer's, store's and reader's options, and the options each searcher, reader and store behind a `Backend` field is built from — `doclet.SearcherOptions`, `doclet.ReaderOptions`, `doclet.Options`, the search fan-out and the engine's item ranker) to a class — `grant`, `value`, `gate` or `none` — so a grant judged from the chart, which being asked last cannot make sound, is never added unseen; and an operation that JUDGES one DECLARES it (`op.judgesGrant`, a predicate over its decoded arguments: `code.read` and `code.resolve_ref` where the asker is a SEAT; `code.change` wherever the chart judges the write, a seat's or one that mentions anybody (`code.ChangeProposal.JudgesChart`); `code.queue` for every enqueue, whoever asks, and a seat's dequeue (`code.QueueProposal.JudgesChart`); `code.merge` for every merge, whoever asks (`code.MergeProposal.JudgesChart`); and `code.conversation` wherever the chart judges the write — a seat's, an ask of reviewers by anybody, or a comment or review that mentions anybody (`code.ConversationWrite.JudgesChart`) — and so wherever a read names the colleague it is made for, which rides beside a seat's asker alone — a person's read consulting no chart; and `code.checks` for a seat's rerun, which judges whether it may write the repository or wrote the change and whoever its turn works for (`code.ChecksRequest.JudgesChart`), a person's rerun and report and the engine's own records consulting none), which such a node answers `behind_config` with the hard arm's own detail EVEN TOLD TO ANSWER ANYWAY — in its server and in this node's own in-process run alike — so the last resort meets the refusal again and the walk ends unserved rather than answer from a revision that may have revoked the grant (M3-O8's hard arm; `TestEveryOperationThatJudgesAGrantIsDeclared` holds every operation on a domain's copy whose arguments carry a `code.Principal` named `Asker` to the declaration, and no git operation to it, whose Gitlet node refuses a seat itself) — and a READ a copy refuses about ITSELF (`statelog.ReadRefusal.Elsewhere`: `behind` a linearizable read's barrier, stalled, deferred, evicted, below the floor, cut off from its broker or a quorum) is asked of the next data node, the refusal the answer only where nobody does better, while `log_full`, `broker_refused` (the one stream every node appends its barrier to refused this one's, sealed or out of resources) and `maintenance`, true of every node alike, are answered at once: returned as the answer, a git fetch through a node whose applier fell a second behind was told 503 while two peers could serve it; and the walk PAYS FOR THE READ ONCE, since every node asked after a refusal is handed what the refusal says it paid for (`statelog.Spent`: the read index its barrier established, which the next node waits for rather than append its own; every position a node waited its whole bound for, a floor among them, which no later node waits for; a log a barrier ran out on, which gets no second barrier), where each node asked afresh appended a barrier to the log they were all behind on and waited a whole read budget, two seconds and a barrier per data node for one final `behind`. The failover rule is PER OPERATION CLASS — a read, a tracker write carrying its operation id, a page or chat write carrying its caller's key (`doclet.Actor.OpKey`, `chatlet.Actor.OpKey`; a seat's always does) and chat's erase and prune under the caller's own id move on, from an `unvouched` answer too, under the same id; a page or chat write with no key (whose op id the store mints per call) reported unanswered is `ErrOutcomeUnknown` and never repeated — and every request carries this node's ONE SESSION-FLOOR table, on the operation's OWN domain's log only (a wake's trigger position among them), so whichever data node answers has applied the node's own writes or says it is behind — and says so while the asker is still listening, because every wait a node makes before answering another (that floor, a read's barrier and level, a write's own record) ends `code.ReplyMargin` short of the asker's deadline (`statelog.WithReplyMargin`): a `behind` sent after the asker stopped waiting is heard as a node that is gone. A read nobody answered, or a walk whose every data node REFUSED, is `ErrUnserved` (a git walk's saying it was the GITLET nodes that could not answer, `ErrUnserved.Git`), never an empty answer — except the knowledge search, which is best effort and answers that it did not run — and it says whether a node it asked WENT SILENT (`Silent`), because a node that refused ran nothing and a silent one may have: a push the walk could not place is `unavailable` only when every node refused it, and `unknown` otherwise; a repeatable write no data node ran, where some data node NEVER ANSWERED, ends in `ErrOutcomeUnknown` naming the silent ones, because such a node may have run it and "nothing ran" is the claim a caller acts on by writing again — the same operation id is the retry. What cannot cross a wire (the chart seams, the lead map, the searching seat's org) is supplied by the SERVING node's epoch, and three gates hold the wire honest: every field an operation's types carry arrives or is named with who supplies it, every sentinel and error type of statelog and of every domain an operation floors on — the executor log's among them, and the identity estate's own (`iam.ErrNoHolder`, `iam.ErrHolderUnseated`, `iamdomain.ErrNotFound`, `session.ErrNoCompany`) — keeps its errors.Is/As identity across it, and the envelope itself is pinned byte for byte. The IDENTITY reads a node without `data` needs are estate operations too, READ-CLASS and floored on the identity log: who holds a login (its binding row, for `iam.Holders`, `iam.OwnerOf` and a Tier A token's seat), who holds each human seat (`SeatHolders`, read whole, for the party registry's standing and a turn's withheld contacts) and who holds ONE, with the holder's grants (`identity.requester`, `Identity.Requester`: two seeks and one document's decode on the serving node, for the person a seat's turn acts for, composed at most once a call, and a new name rather than `identity.seat_holder` reshaped, so a node that does not know it leaves it unserved and no answer is read as a person holding nothing or everything) and the row a presented machine token is checked against (`identity.machine_token`) — the chart and the asking node's own Tier A token list applied on the ASKING side, since neither is the serving node's to know. Each crosses NARROWED: a binding without the row's verifiers and grants (`Binding`), a requester with the grants a turn's ceiling is decided on and nothing else of the person, and a token's row whole but for its VERIFIER, in whose place crosses a MAC over it and a nonce the asker drew for that question alone, under a key both nodes derive from the fleet keyring in a domain of its own (`TokenFacts`; the asker names its active entry and a node holding none runs nothing) — the asker MACs the verifier the presented token implies and takes it only where the two agree, so `credential.CheckToken` stays the one table, neither the secret nor the verifier reaches the broker, and an answer MAC'd for one question verifies under no other question's nonce; the keys ride in `Envelopes`, the one value both halves are handed. CHAT is a floored domain beside them, its search included (the rooms a seat may search are membership rows its own join may just have written): every read crosses with its VIEWER, the seat handle the asking node resolved, inside the signed body, and the SERVING reader decides that seat's rooms from its own membership rows — so a visible set never crosses, and the search resolves it on the node whose index it reads, in one operation that says when that index is still building and names the room each hit was said in, its name and kind from that same set (`ChatSearchAnswer.Rooms`) — while what a caller was admitted to do beyond membership crosses as the asking node's DECISION (`chatlet.MessageAuthority`, `chatlet.ChannelAuthority`), judged on the serving snapshot, and a room's retention is a write of its own rather than a field of a patch; the live channel's room check asks this node's own copy first even while it lags (`Chat.ChannelHere`), never one out of service. THE EXECUTOR LOG is the seventh floored domain (ADR-0073), and its writes are a class of their own: ENGINE-ORIGINATED (`opOrigin`, declared with `byEngine`), the engine's record of what a seat's box did — a turn's first read (`begin`), a capture, an end, the retention's deletes and a removed seat's — which no tool, person or operator surface makes, so `SurfaceWriteDomains` (what `agent/builtin`'s surface declarations are held to) leaves it out — where the code log stays in it, every one of its writes made by a person, a seat's tool or a push and none of its operations declared `byEngine`, the engine-built commit and Gitlet's own sweeps included, since each lands as the push or record its surface would have made — and two gates hold the class: every write on the log is the engine's and nothing else is, and no package serving a person or a model (`agent/builtin`, `api`, `assistant`, `cmd/crewlet`) names the writer facade `ExecutorWrites`, the domain's writer or an engine hand-out of either, by a walk of their source. Each is an idempotent write under the operation the domain derives per execution; its reads (`ExecutorReads`, which a surface may hold) are answered at the caller's level, a launch's conversation read at `linearizable` because a seat that moved holds no floor for the end another node published, and a seat's search of its own sessions (`executor.search`) on the node that holds the rows, which answers its hits alone, a data node of an older build answering it unknown and unserved so the router asks the next; and both facades are exactly the domain's method sets, so the engine cannot tell local from routed. A node in a maintenance mode is served every core half's reader and none of its writers. And every request and every reply is SIGNED under the fleet keyring in a domain of its own (`estate`) and judged by the verdicts a state-log record is (ADR-0031), through `signedask` — the one implementation every instruction channel shares, because the server dispatches a write AS the actor, and answers a chat read FOR the viewer, its envelope claims, and an unsigned channel beside signed records would let anything the broker admitted write as anybody — its admission vouches for a connection, never a request: a key the server does not hold answers that the request DID NOT RUN, so the router moves on, and a tampered envelope is refused and logged. A custody batch is an event envelope rather than an estate request, and stays outside the rule. A push, a compaction, an expunge record and a change's write are the KEYED operations (`op.keyedBy`: `code.propose`, `code.compact`, `code.expunge` — a person's purge request, or a maintainer's begin or commit, keyed by whichever it carries — and `code.change`, an open, an edit, a draft's state, a retarget, a close or a reopen, keyed by the repository its record names, and `code.queue`, an enqueue or a dequeue of a target's merge queue, and `code.merge`, a change's merge as one record its gate decides (ADR-0096), each keyed the same way — and beside them `code.conversation`, a write of a change's conversation, and `code.checks`, a write of a repository's checks — an attempt queued, claimed or ended — each keyed by the same repository and answered by the change writer or the checks writer beside that node's committer, raising this node's session floor but never the repository's own, since neither moves git content — all on the proposals lane, a compaction, an expunge record and a change's write waiting in the repository's one queue beside its pushes): each asked of its repository's committer — the first of `rendezvous.Order(repo id, every live data node)`, this node at its place in that order and never ahead of it, with no sticky node and the same out-of-service and silent demotions every order has — rather than of this node first, so a repository's pushes meet at one committer whichever node received them, and a committer that runs nothing (`code.ErrNotServing`: stopping, a node that publishes nothing, a refusal about itself) hands them to that repository's runner-up with the same push id — or compaction id, which the domain's ledger collapses alike — and is asked LAST for pushes for the `suspectFor` window after (no sticky node moves a keyed order off a node that refused, so every later push re-sent it its whole proposal first); even the lagging last resort asks in the key's order. A repository's GIT WORK is asked of its HOME GITLET NODE instead (ADR-0089, amending ADR-0025): a second placement beside the data nodes, `RouterOptions.Git` (every live node with the gitlet role, off the same watched view; required, an empty one the way to say there is none), for an operation declared `keyedOnGit` on `GitCopy` — no domain's copy, so no copy verdict, no dispatch floor and no lag gate, its floor travelling in its arguments as the Gitlet node's cache's sync level (`CodeSeam.FloorOf` hands it this node's own writes to that repository) — asked in `rendezvous.Order(repo id, every live Gitlet node)` with the keyed order's demotions (a `no_backend` asked last for `suspectFor`, a silent node last of all) and none of the data walk's preferences, never `remembersBehind` or the last resort; this node at its place, in process, where its git half is built (`LocalGit`, resolved PER REQUEST, because Gitlet is built at boot or at the first apply that hosts code, after the router and the server exist), every other Gitlet node on LANES of their own, the reads' and the engine writes' (`laneGitReads` `queue.ConcurrentAnswers` wide, since the node's seat git-work share bounds the git running; `laneGitWrites` HOLDING at most `gitWritesHeld` (64) writes for its peers, mostly through waits that run no git, and `queue.ConcurrentAnswers` wider for the answers it gives AT ONCE — a write past the held ones is answered `behind`, at its share, before its arguments are decoded, never left waiting for a slot in the broker client's buffer, which drops past its 64 MiB, where its asker heard nothing for a whole write attempt and took the busy node for a gone one; a held write holds its request, its admitted copy and its decoded write, about 3 MiB at the payload's bound, measured; registered both or neither, only where `ServerOptions.Git` is set and from boot, answering `no_backend` until Gitlet is built, never silence), its server's git arm after the envelope's admission and the lane check and before the copy's verdict and the readiness gates, one attempt `Timing.GitReadAttempt` (17 s: a share wait, two read budgets, the read's own git's ten seconds of run time and the reply margin, whole; the read lane's queue and the short checks of what a read names are left out and come out of the attempt), each attempt SERVED UNTIL ITS ANSWER IS DUE, a reply's margin before it ends (`code.AnswerBy`) — the git arm for a peer and this node's own half in process alike, the in-process run held to the same attempt — so every wait the read makes ends there and is answered unready while the asker still listens: served to the request's deadline and merely marked with the margin, which nothing on the git path reads, a read waiting on its share or a slot answered after its asker gave up, and the asker suspected a busy node and sent its repositories' reads to a runner-up that downloaded each. A Gitlet node that cannot answer for a reason about ITSELF (`code.ErrGitUnready`: syncing, its share, no chart, behind its configuration, a failure of its own, or no copy held) answers `behind` — `behind_config` for a seat on a node behind its configuration, the node's posture, which the asker remembers for its data operations too — with the reason beside it (`reply.Unready`), never an error on the wire, and is NOT demoted — the syncing home is the right node a moment later — and ONE node a walk FILLS a copy at a time: the walk stamps its effective home's attempt (`code.GitQuery.Home`, the first node once the demotions apply) and every other Gitlet node holding none answers `not_held` having started nothing, so a repository nobody holds costs the fleet one download, never one a Gitlet node; the fill moves to the next node of the walk only past a node bringing no copy up for the read (`code.UnreadyReason.PassesFill`: behind its configuration, a failure of its own, not serving Gitlet), never past one that may be filling — kept on the first node, a home stuck behind a revision left every seat unable to read a repository it alone held — and never past a home at its share, which holds its copy and is only busy: the share is the node's, so a repository's seat reads are bounded by the shares of the nodes holding a copy of it. `Router.Home` names a repository's home — the node its reads and engine writes are asked of first, and the one its maintenance falls back to — the first node of the git walk's order with NO demotion, through the one function every keyed order is built by (`Router.keyed`), so on a quiet fleet the home and the reads' first node never disagree, and a home that went quiet is still the home, answered or the error of a placement that could not be read (`ErrNoGitletNode` where it lists no Gitlet node), never a guess. A home's own work is its repositories' CHANGE WORK (`code/home`) — a repository's compaction and publication are its maintainer's (ADR-0091) — and `Router.GitOrder` answers a repository's WHOLE git order — every live Gitlet node in its rendezvous order, the home first, with no demotion — which a check's claim is ranked by on every Gitlet node alike and a running check's runner is judged present by (internal/code/checkrun); `Router.HomeOf` answers which of MANY repositories this node is the home of off ONE reading of who serves git — what the home loop's backstop pass asks once over its workers' listings, which asked one repository at a time read the presence view, decoded every node's lease and sorted the Gitlet nodes for each — three-valued: the set, or for every one the error of a placement that could not be read (`ErrNoGitletNode` where it lists no Gitlet node), so a node that cannot tell does none of a home's work. `Router.GitOrders` is `GitOrder` of MANY repositories off ONE reading, for HomeOf's reason — a code search's scatter (`codesearch`) assigns every repository an asker may read, up to `config.CodeMaxRepos` of them, to the first node of its order and its runner-up to the second, and a reading a repository would read the presence view again for each and could place one scatter on a fleet that moved part way through it. `Router.Maintainer(repoID, charge)` is the Gitlet node a repository's MAINTENANCE — the compaction of its packs, the publication of its layers — is placed on: the first of the SAME order (`Router.keyed`, the rendezvous order Home reads, still with no demotion) whose ADVERTISED background budget holds the charge (each Gitlet node's `coord.GitBackgroundKey`, which its presence row carries on every beat BESIDE its status, so a beat whose status read overran still says it), else the home — the order and every figure read off ONE LISTING (`GitPlacement.Listing`, the git placement's `RouterOptions.Git`: the Gitlet nodes and what each says, read together), so a node is weighed by the listing that names it rather than ordered off one listing and weighed off the next a refresh put in its place, and a node that listing does not carry — this one included, wherever its own git half is built — is GONE, never not saying; so on alike nodes the maintainer IS the home, and on a fleet with one large Gitlet node every repository only it can hold is maintained there; NOTHING MOVES PAST THE HOME ON MISSING INFORMATION: a node whose row carries no figure is NOT SAYING, never one with nothing to give, and is passed over where it is a runner-up — kept in its place, a small runner-up not saying would take a large node's repositories, each beginning with a cold sync of its whole history only for its own admission to refuse the work — and keeps the repositories it is home to, as a quiet home keeps them, since the home holds their copies and a quiet home that cannot hold the work costs that repository its pass, refused at its admission over the copy it already holds; `Router.MaintainerOf` answers which of MANY repositories, each at its own charge, this node maintains off ONE listing for them all — what a maintainer's two passes ask once over their due listings, which asked one repository at a time read the presence view, decoded every node's lease and sorted the Gitlet nodes for each — three-valued: the set, or for every one a listing that could not be read, UNKNOWN, or one that carries no Gitlet node, `ErrNoGitletNode`; `Router.Maintainer` and `MaintainerOf` judge through one function (`maintainerOver`), so the two can never disagree; and `Router.Listed` is whether that listing carries THIS node at all — by the listing, never by its git half — which a maintainer's two loops wait on before their first pass, since a booting node is listed only once its host beats. Gitlet reaches it through `Router.Code()` (`CodeSeam`), which raises this node's floor only for its OWN writes — a proposal that landed, a push's, a compaction's or an expunge record's, and a push it proposed found landed — never for a read's position, and raises it TWICE: the session's on the whole code log, which every routed code operation carries, and the written repository's own (`FloorOf`, `repoFloors`), which a read by object id of that repository carries and a read of any other does not — floored at the session's, a push to one repository made every other's home sync for nothing on every read. The node keeps `config.CodeMaxRepos` repositories' floors, forgetting the lowest past it, which costs a read of that repository at most the Gitlet node's one sync at the log's head. A MERGE PREVIEW (`code.merge_preview`, `opCodeMergePreview`, `CodeSeam.MergePreview`) is a git READ like a read by object id — the same walk, the reads' lane and attempt, its attempt stamped home, a node that cannot answer saying `behind` with its reason — answered by the git half's `GitServer.MergePreview` (the merge a repository's home records a change's mergeability by, `code/home`), its floor the query's own, raising none. An ENGINE WRITE (`code.git_write`, `opCodeGitWrite`, `CodeSeam.GitWrite`) walks the same git order as an `opIdempotentWrite` keyed by its push id — derived from its caller's operation, so the runner-up asked the same write after a node that ran nothing (`code.ErrNotServing`, declined and asked last) or went silent builds the same push and is answered from its row where the silent node landed it — held to the one rule every party to a write holds it to (`code.EngineWrite.Validate`) before any node is asked, and raising this node's floors only where it applied or is pending; its attempt on one Gitlet node, `Timing.GitWriteAttempt` (82 s: a share wait, three read budgets, the build's ten seconds, the upload's allowance, the proposal's own attempt and the margin, whole; every term's p99 measured beside its budget by BenchmarkEngineWrite, inside each but the share's wait, which sixty-four writes on a one-unit share reach whole and are sent on unready, and every answer's p99 3.2 s at the most), is the router's own whatever deadline its caller gives (`budgetFor`), since the Gitlet node fits every stage into it and only a wedged one costs it, and `NewRouter` refuses one no longer than the proposal's attempt and the margin. The router's attempt budgets — a read's and a write's on one data node, a git read's and an engine write's on one Gitlet node, and the admission question's whole — are ONE `Timing` (`RouterOptions.Timing`), `Production()` on every node, so a suite in another package can scale a WEDGED node's cost without reaching an unexported field (a node that is gone costs no attempt: nothing serves its subject). A shorter attempt never hears an honest node as silent — the serving node fits its waits into whatever attempt it is given, a reply's margin short of it — so `NewRouter` refuses only a field left zero by name and an attempt that cannot do its job: a read attempt no longer than `code.ReplyMargin`, which leaves the serving node no time to wait for anything or run the read, and a write attempt no longer than the floor wait, a committer's batch and its answer (`code.MinProposeAttempt`: `statelog.ReadBudget` + `code.CommitBudget` + `code.ReplyMargin`, 33 s — the domain's ONE sum of what a proposal needs, which Gitlet holds an engine write's upload to as well, so the two never disagree), under which a push whose committer first waited out its floor is answered busy, undecided. Production's ten-second read attempt is a linearizable read's waits at their whole budgets and the margin (2 + 5 + 2 + 1). A repository's readers are ONE PAGE A ROUTED CALL (`Usage.RepoReaders` over `usage.repo_reads`, with `usage.repo_reads_elided` on the first page; both floorless): the asker's page budget travels with the call, capped by the serving node's, every data node cuts and resumes by the one rule, a page that does not end after its cursor is refused, and a cursor or a range no read takes crosses the wire as its sentinel. A REPOSITORY LIFECYCLE REQUEST (`code.lifecycle`, `opCodeLifecycle`) is routed to any data node like a settings change and DECIDED THERE against that node's own chart and configuration (`judgesGrant`, its predicate true for every request, since every one names its actor and is judged by its grant), so a node confirmed behind refuses it `not_serving` and the asker tries another; the asker's floor is raised only by an answer that carries a record (`applied`, or `pending` at its position). `code.mark` is the one UNKEYED code write: a person's code inbox mark, asked of any data node, whose writer refuses it for anybody but the person. An ENGINE WRITE'S ATTEMPT FOLLOWS ITS KIND (`op.attemptBy`, `Timing.GitWriteAttemptFor`): the git write attempt with its build term, `code.WriteBuildDeadline`, replaced by the kind's own build budget, so a `merge_change` — landed as one merge record, its build a mergeability's thirty seconds — is given 102 s on one Gitlet node, a `rebase_change`, replaying up to a thousand commits under forty, 112 s, and every other kind its 82, read off the write each attempt of the walk carries, its home's included. |
| `rendezvous` | THE ONE ORDER A FLEET'S NODES ARE PREFERRED IN FOR A KEY — rendezvous (highest-random-weight) hashing, ADR-0008's rule applied to placement. `Order(key, nodes)` ranks every node by a 64-bit weight of the pair and nothing else exists to agree on: no table to build, publish or keep current, every node computing the same order from the same SET (a tie breaks on the node's own bytes, so the order a placement listed them in never matters), and a membership change moving only what it must — a node that leaves hands each key it ranked first to that key's own runner-up, spread across the survivors, and one that joins takes about 1/N of the keys while nothing else moves. The weight is FNV-1a over `key NUL node` FINISHED by MurmurHash3's fmix64, and the finisher is the point: plain FNV-1a ranked nodes named alike but for a last character — `node-0`…`node-4`, a StatefulSet's ordinals — by that character's low bits, so one of five nodes came first for half of all keys and every other node had ONE fixed runner-up (`node-0`'s was always `node-1`), which sent all of a failed node's load to a single neighbour. GOLDEN VECTORS pin the arithmetic, because two builds in a rolling upgrade that rank one key differently disagree about which node it prefers, and the weight is deliberately unexported, because comparing two weights anywhere else is a second order. Its caller is `estate`'s router, in TWO walks keyed on two different things. Every operation any data node answers equally is keyed on the asking node's own id, and what it takes from the order is an asker's FIRST data node and every failover target — spread evenly — and never where the asker STAYS: the router keeps asking the node that last answered until that node goes silent, so a data node that joins is asked only by askers with none yet or whose node went silent. A push — the one KEYED operation — is keyed on its REPOSITORY'S id over every live data node, the asker included where it holds the estate, and there the order is the whole decision: no node is stayed on, and its first node is the repository's committer, where every asker's pushes to it meet so one group commit holds a burst — and a committer that leaves hands each repository to that repository's own runner-up, spread over the survivors. `TestNoPackageOrdersByAHashOfItsOwn` holds it as the only implementation: any other package that ORDERS two values derived from a hash — a comparison, a `cmp`/`bytes`/`strings` compare, `min`/`max`, a sort, max or search over hash values — is rendezvous or a hash ring whatever its candidates are called, and that includes a hash SCALED by `/` or a `math` function (weighted rendezvous ranks by `-w/ln(u)`) and RAW digests in their canonical byte order (a sorted set of SHA-256 sums is a ring's points, and `bytes.Compare` over two of them is rendezvous over SHA-256), however the comparator reaches them; while a digest compared for equality or encoded into a name, a hash WRAPPED into a bucket by `%`, `&` or `math.Mod` (`search.ShardOf`), a seed or a one-sided threshold never is |
| `objstore` | The OBJECT STORE — ADR-0026 — and its vocabulary: ONE OBJECT PER UPLOAD, under a `Key` minted for that upload alone — a UUIDv7, strictly parsed, built by `KeyAt` from the store's own clock, carrying the instant it was minted and never minted twice — and an `Object` (key, the whole content's SHA-256 `Hash`, size) that a row names. A key is never derived from the content: content addressing made two files share a stored copy, and a shared copy is one a writer can be re-using at the moment the collector deletes it — so there is NO DEDUPE (a move uploads its bytes again; the seat's own write skips content the file already holds) and NO LOCK. What is divided off is the BYTES and only the bytes: that a file exists, its path, its hash and its object's key are replicated rows like everything else, so listing a project's files never leaves the node. The bytes live in ONE `Backend` the whole fleet shares (`Put`, `Get`, `Stat`, `Delete`, `List`, plus `Pending`/`Abandon` for the uploads it began and never finished, every verb certified by `objstoretest`) — a DUMB, STREAMING store of opaque names: a put reads a reader to its END — `io.EOF` itself, through `Fill`, the one rule every reader in pieces here follows, never a body cut short's `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`, which `io.ReadFull` answers for its own short read too and so stored the half of an upload that arrived as the whole — and leaves nothing anybody can find when it fails or is abandoned, a get hands back a reader and REFUSES a context with no deadline rather than pick a bound of its own, and a listing hands back every name it holds verbatim and never one it cannot DATE (`ErrUndated`), because what a name means is this package's grammar and the collector's judgement and never a backend's. Every name the engine writes is `files/<key>` (`Key.Name`), so a shared bucket's other objects are never the engine's. It is wrapped in a `Store` that mints the key, counts and hashes every byte on the way in (the size limit and a cancelled context reaching the backend as a FAILED READ, the one failure every backend cleans up after), and on the way out checks every byte against the row and HOLDS BACK THE BYTE THAT COMPLETES THE FILE until the whole is verified — so a download of a damaged object ends short rather than whole, and `ErrCorrupt` is only a DEFINITE answer, never a read that failed first. A read is bounded by `ReadBudget` and ended by `Stall` when its backend stops moving — or has begun no stream, since the backend's open is a wait on it like any Read and a backend asking a failed request again until its deadline would otherwise hold a read its whole budget; and a WRITE the backend stops taking is ended at the same minute by the backend that sends it, the only one that can see it move (`ErrStalled` either way: the store failing, never a refusal); a page (`ReadAt`) is checked for its length only. `RecordWithin` (12 h) is the bound on the write that names a key, which is what lets the collector delete with no lock. `AssumedClockSkew` (1 h) is the most a node's clock, or the clock of the broker member leading the position register, may stand from the fleet's — the median of the data nodes' clocks; the engine's `clock_skew` raises past it — so two machines may disagree by TWICE it, the reading every rule that judges one machine's instant by another machine's clock is held to: the collector's grace against `RecordWithin`, and a retired reference's against its longest read, since the node sweeping a retired row and the broker member that stamped its retirement are each held only to the fleet's clock. `MiBPace` is the ONE floor a transfer is held to on every leg — the API's upload and download pacing, a bucket request, an object read — so no bound can be retuned out from under another. A backend that lists its names IN ORDER implements `Ranged` (`ListRange(after, through)`, certified by `objstoretest`, which refuses an uncertified one), and `Store.ListKeys` reads it as keys and CHECKS the order rather than trusting it (`ErrUnordered`), because every caller reads an object missing from a range as one the store does not hold; `Key.Compare` is the order of the canonical spelling. One that deletes many names in one request implements `BatchDeleter` (`DeleteBatch`, at most `MaxDeleteBatch` (1,000) names — S3's DeleteObjects — certified the same way), read through `Store.DeleteKeys`, which counts what the store says it removed (`DeleteBatchError` names each name it refused) and answers `ErrNoBatch` for a store that refused the request itself, a gateway without the verb, so its caller deletes each name instead. Two OPTIONAL CAPABILITIES a backend may advertise rather than verbs every backend must answer: `Presigner` (the s3 backend, once its probe proved the provider enforces the bindings), through which `Store.PresignPut` signs a client's own put of a key the store minted (`Store.Mint`), bound to length, type, SHA-256 and `If-None-Match: *`, ending inside `RecordWithin` and at most `MaxPresignTerm` (`PresignTerm` sizes it), and answering `ErrDirectUnavailable` everywhere else; and `Reserver` (the nats bucket), whose `Usage` the store reports. A put that bucket refuses because its reservation is spent is `ErrFull` — and so is one an S3-compatible bucket's provider refuses for want of room — a REFUSAL rather than a failure, answered only inside a `Full` that carries the BACKEND'S OWN remedy — the room is made where the backend keeps its bytes, which only the backend knows: every surface refusing an upload for it says so in its own vocabulary and splices in that `Remedy`, keeps the store's own words (its bucket, its keys) for the log, and never invites the retry the full store answers the same. `ReferenceTable` is how a consumer DECLARES a table that names objects, its two statements decoded once beside them, and the declarations live in `objstore/references` rather than beside either end, because the collector deletes whatever no declared table names. A Required declaration also names the LOG that writes it, the table its domain DEFERS that log's unreadable records into, and the domain's own reader of ONE RECORD (`Records`, sharing the applier's decoder, the row spelled with `JoinOwner` exactly as the walk spells it), because a backup carries what the log a restore replays names (ADR-0082); `ErrRecordUnreadable` is a newer build's record that may name an object, and `ValidateLog` refuses a Required table missing any of the three. The KEYSET WALK of a declared table (`WalkOf`, a `WalkPage` of 500 rows a read, each reference carrying its table's standing) and the K-WAY MERGE of every walk into one key order (`MergeWalks`, one page of each table held, a key two rows name handed on adjacent) are here too, once, for every pass that reads them — the audit, the backup and a store move. A declaration's STANDING is one of three, ADR-0081, with no default: `Required` (kept from collection, audited, copied, counted and asked after by a backup, copied by a store move), `Retired` (kept for its domain's grace and nothing else) and `Derived` (kept while a row names it and copied by a store move, never audited, never copied, counted or asked after by a backup — an object the engine can build again, so it owes no grace, and a backup taken again and again would pay its bytes every time to spare a rare rebuild, where a move made once would leave every node of the moved fleet to rebuild it); the obligations are one table at `Standing`'s doc, the collector asks every table, and each walk is built for its `Pass` (`PassAudit`, `PassBackup`, `PassMove`), whose `Reads` is the table's walk columns: the audit's and the backup's read `Required` alone and refuse the other two, a store move's reads `Required` and `Derived` and refuses a retired table, whose rows no pass walks (`ReferencesAfter` refuses it). The first `Derived` objects are a repository's PUBLISHED LAYERS (ADR-0091): built once by its maintainer, installed by every Gitlet node only once checked against their rows, and published again after a restore, since no backup carries one |
