A node serving Gitlet ANSWERS THE FLEET'S CODE STATUS on `crewlet.code.status` (`codestatus.go`) with `host.Server.Status`, registered once the host starts and withdrawn first inside the host's one bounded stop, so no peer is told of a cache that is going; UNSIGNED, since a node answers it about itself and carries nothing out for the asker (internal/signedask's rule), and versioned, a question at a version this build does not speak answered by nobody; a question NAMES the Gitlet nodes that answer it (`nodes`, none named asking every one) and says whether they send their hot lists (`without_hot`), both additive at protocol 1, so a node it does not name answers nothing before it reads its status and a page of a few Gitlet nodes is answered by those few. ANY node ASKS it, for `code_status`, in two steps: `GitletNodes`, the Gitlet nodes the presence leases list live (a read of the coordination store, no node asked), and `CodeStatus`, a scatter of the nodes the tool's page names — or of every Gitlet node, naming none, for the fleet's first page and its hot list — inside the fleet read budget (`eventfan.FleetReadBudget`), lasting until every node it ASKED has answered — never a count of replies, because a node it did not ask can answer too (an older build answers whatever the question names, a draining one a question naming nobody), and such a reply is dropped — reported with the one coverage shape every fanned answer carries over the nodes asked — a Gitlet node that did not answer, or answered at a version this build does not read, is named rather than counted healthy, and a node with no broker asks its own host. The health tools take `HealthToolDeps` on both surfaces — the presence leases with the requester ceiling's halves beside them (`turnRequesters`, `ChartAuthorityOf`, read per call), so `fleet_health` in a turn somebody woke reads only for somebody of the company who may act — and a seat's runner is handed the builtins its seat is refused outright (`RunnerFor` takes the context and asks `builtin.Withheld` over the runner's own registry, as the seat's principal, against the epoch it pins), so what a seat is offered and what it is admitted are one decision — and the code writes too where the seat's code tier writes no repository (`builtin.CodeWritesWithheld` over that epoch's role, `code.Tier(role.CodeAccess)` as `codeRoster` reads it): every call of one would be refused by every repository's grant, which the authority table, admitting everybody to a code write so each repository's grant decides it, cannot say ahead of the calls. A data node's ALARM TRANSITIONS leave through an OUTBOX (`alarmwakes.go`, armed with the retention loops and stopped with them): the tracker hands each one on as it is made, and the outbox publishes it as the inbound delivery `alarmwake` routes (source `alarms`), retried until the broker takes it — two seconds doubling to the alarm interval — and in order, bounded at 1024 with the oldest not in flight dropped and counted (`crewlet.alarm.transitions.dropped`, the taken ones on `crewlet.alarm.transitions{change}`); a transition still queued when the node stops is not recovered, since the next start's first evaluation says what is still firing. The alarms' parser rides `nativeParsers` on every node, whatever halves it runs, built per epoch from the chart's granted seats. Gitlet's (`code.NewParser`, `code.Prompt`) rides it where the company hosts its repositories (`halves.code`), its wakes relayed by the code log's feed the register's code entry declares (`crewlet-code-feed`), and `code.Prompt` is one of `workItemNamers`, so a code wake charges its turn to the work item the change implements (ADR-0097). WHO A SEAT'S TURN IS ACTING FOR IS COMPOSED ONCE (`turnRequesters`, requesters.go), handed to the seat's registry (`builtin.Deps.Requesters`, equip.go) and to the families that decide a relation beside it (`ArtifactToolDeps`, `CodeToolDeps`, each read per call) — an agent seat as its own principal, every app and never admin, and a person's seat as the person the routed identity directory says holds it, at their stage, holding the apps their grants name and never admin (ADR-0109): that one seat's requester (`Identity.Requester`), never the whole directory, because it is composed at most once a call; a removed holder, a stage that may not act and a seat no person holds use no app — so one requester is one principal whichever tool decides for it. WHO WOKE IT is read off the trigger by one resolution (`subjectOf`, prefetch.go) for the requester, the senders and every counterparty profile alike: a vendor's sender as an id in its own namespace, and a FIRST-PARTY notice's writer by the kind its record holds (`types.NotificationWriter`, `writerSubject`) — a seat's change, or a person's as their seat, that seat by its handle; the engine's own, nobody; a credential acting as no seat, its platform identity and its LOGIN, the requester the turn is then worked for by the apps every one of its writes carried (`credentialRequesterOf`, onto `turnctx.Turn.RequesterLogin`/`RequesterApps` and the parked run's row), narrowed again per call by what THIS node resolves the login to (`turnRequesters.Credential`: a `token:` login by this node's Tier A alone, any other by the directory alone, ADR-0109); a removed seat or an unknown kind, the platform identity a stranger keeps — because the tracker's and the knowledge base's actor is spelled as a handle, a login or a node's name alike, and read as a vendor id every colleague's comment woke a stranger's turn. The requester is the first voice besides the seat's OWN (`requesterOf`): the outcome of its own act asks it nothing, and a colleague who speaks after it is who the turn is for. THE LIVE TURNS' CODE HOLDS (codeholds.go, M3-decisions M3-O61, M3-O64) — the scratch repositories and the seats' branches a turn named, by keys this package never decodes: a turn's `turnctx.Holds` lives in this process while it runs — every running turn in one registry (`runningTurns`), entered by the dispatch and a resume for the turn's whole run — and on its RUN ROW once it launches (`sandbox.PendingRun.CodeHolds`): both launch paths write the set on the row they open and attach the row's writer through `Opened` (the seal), and a resumed turn starts from the row's set (`rowHolds`), so a parked run holds what its turn named until its row ends; a coding box's push adds the seats' branches it names to the same row (`boxRuns.Hold`), because a box pushes as its run and never as a turn, and a row that is gone or ending holds nothing new and is no error, since a run that has ended depends on nothing. `Engine.codeHolds` is the code-retention pass's `Retention.Holds`: every run row, whatever its status (`ListRuns`) — listed BEFORE and AGAIN AFTER the ask, because a turn's first launch moves its holds from its memory onto a new row while the ask is on its way, and a row written after the first listing by a turn whose frame returned before the ask reached its node was in neither answer — and every seat-lease holder's running turns, asked on `crewlet.code.holds` (an unsigned ephemeral read scatter inside `eventfan.FleetReadBudget`, lasting until every holder the leases NAME has answered — never a count of replies, because every node answers it, one holding no seat among them, and its answer would fill the count while a holder's went unread) — the seat holders, never the presence listing, because a draining node gives its presence back before its turns finish — and a store, a lease read or a holder that cannot be read is an error, so a page expires nothing on an unknown. The box credentials are built at `New` on EVERY node over the fleet keyring, whatever its roles: a coding box's run tokens (`BoxTokens`) and a check's box's tokens (`CheckTokens`), in one key domain — the node that launches a run or claims a check mints, whichever Gitlet node the box dials verifies, and the API verifies either on a node where Gitlet is not built (`api.CodeSurface.VerifyBox`) — and Gitlet admits both by them (`host.Boxes`). A `direct` or `container` box is its launching node's (`sandboxhost.go`): every node runs a waiter of its own for the boxes on its host beside the fleet's, answers a peer's signed read of one of them (`sandbox.box_read`, only what the run's row licenses) and listens for the nudges (`crewlet.sandbox.nudge`) its waiters act on — a run's `submit_work` recorded by the bridge ledger, a box left to its host — and the fleet's waiter reads the presence leases to find a node gone for good. The sandbox coordinator holds this process's TAKER LEASE (`coordinatorOptions`): the node's own lease store, through `holdLeases`, whose give-back is a step of the stop's one allowance once the teardown has begun — the coordinator gives it back on the lifetime it claimed it on, which no stop's context reaches — the engine's incarnation and the seat lease TTL in force, none of the three without the store, and `stopSandbox`, called by the teardown alone, after the drain, which keeps the lease while presence is gone, stops it only once its last keep has ended (`TestTheSandboxIsStoppedOnlyByTheTeardownAfterTheDrain` holds the order from the source); the runtime is built and published under one lock (`publishSandbox`), never built to lose a compare-and-swap, since a second coordinator would claim the same lease at the same epoch and give it back under the published one's keeps. A node's MODEL STATE is gathered for its heartbeat (`modelstate.go`: each entry's sign-in plan, the parks naming it, the login watcher of `hostlogin.go`) and its executor cells probed (`runnerprobe.go`); a person's retry is a coordination record every node applies by its stamp (`modelretry.go`), a device sign-in one record per model whose process runs on one node (`devicesignin.go`), and a run refused on a sign-in replaced while it ran is carried on once (`signInReplaced`). The model alarms' and the MCP alarms' inputs are fleet-wide, read off ONE listing of the presence leases per evaluation that carries the last good one across a blip (`modelalarms.go`, `mcpalarms.go`); an MCP server's heartbeat row names the instance its `down_since` and `waiting_since` date, so its failure and its outage are one instance's facts. WHAT ITS MCP SERVERS LIST is derived off its bridges at every beat and written only when it moved, under its presence epoch, schemas first; every node keeps a watched copy of the fleet's listings, which the tool catalogue adds a per-agent server's tools from and which a server's detail reads, and the maintenance sweep removes what no reader counts (`mcplistings.go`, ADR-0074). HOW EACH INSTANCE IS stays in the node's memory and is read off ONE reading of each instance (`mcpReadings`) by both the heartbeat's row and a server's page, which asks the nodes holding one over `crewlet.observe.mcp_instances` within the history read's two-second budget (`mcpinstances.go`, the ADR-0021 pattern). A PERSON'S RESTART is a coordination record every node watches and applies once per stamp to the instances it runs whose state began before it, a seat's by its holder alone, and the apply that removes a server or seat deletes it (`mcprestart.go`). A PERSON'S TEST of a server is asked of the nodes that run it over a SIGNED channel (`mcp.check`, since the node asked starts a process or dials as the company), every live node for a shared server and only the node that proves it holds the seat for a per-agent one, each testing with the values a start of it would get (`resolveServer`, `serverSpec`) and answering a bounded, redacted report; a saved server's test is recorded as its latest (`coord.MCPCheck`) and swept with the server, a draft's never (`mcpcheck.go`). EXECUTOR SESSIONS (`executorsession.go`, ADR-0073): the sandbox runtime keeps each launch's session and records every turn's end through the estate router's `ExecutorWrites` (`Engine.executorLog`, set in `New` — never a data node's own writer, since a seat's box is wherever its seat runs), with `executorKeep` (the switch and the per-seat budget off the FLEET's revision, the keyring the secrets a capture scrubs by value are sealed under — references resolved, the entry's sign-in, its login's strings, and every token an integration issues the seat, at the launch and as the completion poll renews it in a running box, which `refreshTokenFiles` records before it writes (`recordToken` through the waiters' `Record`, `sandbox.Coordinator.RecordHanded`), a token the store does not take not written on that poll — the turn's mint by `rebaseFor`, the sealed put). Every way a turn that launched its executor ends records its END, OWED on the run's record (`oweExecutorEnd`) for the run's ending to record: the resume's (`recordResume`, a stop its own fence met, an abandon — a relaunch that failed in its launch included, whose record waits for the frame — and a panic once begun, `resumeGuarded`), and the coordinator's for EVERY stop of a run, parked, launching or before its park, and every loss (`closeStoppedTurn`, `answerLostTurn`, which read delivery with `turn.Answered` off the run's bridged log the coordinator read for the ending and hands them, a log it could not read being `DeliveryUnknown`, never "did not reply") — a frame whose launch a stop decided on the run ended (`stoppedByRun`) answers and owes nothing. Only a frame that finds no record left — a dispatch's launch its own fence refused once its record was written — records the end at once (`endTurnNow`). `answerColleague` reports what it sent and whether the reply went. A launch's secrets for its session's scrub are the engine's to name, by where each value came from (`launchSecrets`, `referencedValues`). AN MCP SERVER SIGNED IN TO WITH OAUTH (`mcpoauth.go`, ADR-0075) has one grant for the company: a sign-in started on any node (`StartMCPSignIn`) is a state signed under the fleet keyring and spent once by whichever node the vendor returns the browser to (`CompleteMCPSignIn`), the refresh token sealed in `fleetsecrets.Estate` and the public half a `coord.MCPGrant`; each node's access token is held in its memory by a per-grant source (`bearerFor`) the shared-server pass hands the spec, only while the server's address is the resource the grant was issued for, renewed under the fleet's `mcp_oauth_renewal` lease and written back at the version read, a refusal for good recorded so no node asks again; a sign-out or a removal revokes at the vendor and deletes (`RevokeMCPGrant`), and a sign-in or sign-out re-activates the revision. A SERVICE IDENTITY (`oauth.grant: client_credentials`, `mcpserviceidentity.go`) is the same source with another way to be issued a token: nobody signs in, nothing is kept and no lease is taken (nothing shared is spent), each node signs in as the company's own client when a request needs a token, reading the token endpoint from the server's metadata, and holds a failure for the restart schedule's wait (`serviceIdentity.issue`), a new id, secret or scope list being a new source asked at once. `resolveServer` holds a server back whose own client's secret does not resolve. A test that sends what it tests (a draft, or a value with its entry as the fleet's active revision states it, so no node needs to have applied the write) sends the entry and every value sealed apart under the fleet's keyring, bound to its request (`mcpEntryAAD`, `mcpValueAAD`, wire version 3), never recorded. |

## The agent runtime

| Package | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `agent/turn` | The turn loop — an executor and a reviewer — the guards around them, and the one question the whole engine turns on: did this turn actually reach anybody? WHO IS WAITING is derived at dispatch from the trigger's own type and WHAT RAN is the tool loop's own record, so neither half is something a model can get wrong. It replaced a reconciliation of the planner's PREDICTED tools against reality, which is where both recorded delivery incidents came from. WHAT RAN includes what the run's record could not keep: a round's elided middle (`Work.Elided`) is read by every delivery check as calls by name and outcome (`Work.Called`, `Record`, a closed round's too) and closes with the round (`ledger.Iteration.Elided`), so a reply posted from the middle of a long run is never refuted and sent back to be posted again |
| `agent/runner` | Drives the phases against real models and real tools — the wiring between the prompt builder, the tool registry, the provider chain and the turn loop's contract, none of which knows the others. Plumbing, plus the one rule plumbing cannot express: what happens when the model never gives a structured answer at all. What a valid answer IS lives here too, in the decoders; the SHAPE is `agent/structured`. Every phase is a harness's own loop over the seat's tools, and every phase but the executor runs on this host, served from the process's one tool-session host (`Config.Sessions`, required — a runner with none is refused before any turn). The executor is ONE runtime (`agentrun.go`): its harness's own agentic run in a box — the launch, which parks the turn, and the collection, which replays the run's bridged calls, in the order the bridge admitted them, through the run's surface rebuilt as the run left it to recover the submission it made, with the same prompt, the same surface, the same submission and the same rescue as every phase, and only the rounds happening in the harness. The run's log keeps each call to its share of the log, so the live `submit_work` refuses a submission past what the log keeps whole (`keptWhole`, `sandbox.MaxSubmissionBytes`), and the replay never replays a newest submission the log kept in part (`BridgedCall.ArgsBytes`): the round is rescued rather than reported with a marker as its summary. Every segment that re-enters a run SEEDS the turn's call log BY IDENTITY (`seedCalls`): each kept call by its digest, each call the log dropped from a long run's middle by its tallied identity (`Resume.Elided`), each call a bridged call's own work made — a `delegate`'s workers, which count on the call's own log (`subagent.Tool.CallForTurn`) — by its tallied identity too (`Resume.Absorbed`), a call whose arguments the record withholds (a held call and the one a person approved) as an unknown call of its tool, and the closed rounds' calls and both their tallies likewise, so a cut argument, a dropped call or a worker's call never moves an operation id a later call derives. A person's answer to a run's question CARRIES THE RUN ON (`asked.go`, `Resume.Asked`) rather than being reported to the turn: the run continues the asking job's kept session (`continued.go`) or, where it was not kept, its own in its kept box, or starts afresh told the question, the answer and its branch. A reply in the conversation it asked in reaches it inside a fence of the relaunching turn's token, labelled as the reply's trigger labels the message (ADR-0040); an answer given by turn reaches it defused and unfenced, as the instruction of the person who gave it. So does a job LOST with its host (`lost.go`, `Resume.Lost`): the same round relaunched in the lost job's kept session where its launcher says it can — the capture its loss's read took where its box was left — told it was cut off (`Lost.Continuation`), and in a fresh session otherwise and after a second loss in the round, told it was cut off, why and where to look for its work — unless the round's calls already hold its submission, which collects it — and refused past its limit with `ErrRoundLost`, closing the round's phase failed. A node that recovers a run still RUNNING — after a restart or a move — rebuilds its surface from the turn's parked state and the calls already in the run's log (`ReopenAgentRun`), so the next call's operation id carries on from them. Every segment that re-enters a run — its collection, an answer or a loss carrying it on, a reopen — makes ONE rebuild (`rebuiltSurface`): the tools and skills the launch recorded — the skills only where the job's box said it took up the session its launch chose (`Resume.Continued`, off the job's record; `Resume.parked`), none where it started its own or said nothing — then every skill its own job loaded over the bridge (past `execstate.State.BridgeFrom`), and the turn's call log seeded with the round's calls; a relaunch then re-arms its guard for the session it takes up, as the launch decides (`sessionDecided`), and empties it again where the run's box says, before the run's first call, that it started a session of its own instead (`AgentRunRequest.Started`, `sessionStarted`; a run taken over is told the same through `ReopenedRun.Started`). AN EXECUTOR HOLDS EVERY TOOL ITS SEAT DOES from its launch (`executorActive`) — every MCP server's but those that run in its box — and no discovery pair (`discovers`): its harness keeps a large server's tools out of its requests itself, so a run activates nothing and its record lists nothing left to discover. The collection calls nothing through its surface, and is rebuilt the same way all the same. And the surface's own METER (`BridgedSpend`), because the harness calls the seat's tools after the segment that launched it has charged what it spent, so what those calls cost (the auxiliary rewrites, the delegated workers) is counted apart, written to the run's row with every bridged call and paid by the segment that resumes. A seat's WITHHELD builtins (`Config.Withheld`: the tools the authority table refuses that seat outright, computed by the engine once per runner from the epoch it pins) leave the registry's snapshot through ONE method every phase reads (`seatSnapshot`) — the executor in either runtime and on a resume, the reviewer, the onboarding turn and the workers a phase hands its tools to — so a seat is never shown a tool whose every call it would be refused. The DISCOVERY PAIR (`list_mcp_server_tools`, `activate_tool`) never passes through the registry, so `DiscoveryTools` hands it out as ENTRIES carrying their own hints — read-only, idempotent, closed-world — which every phase surface and a worker's (`subagent.Config.Discovery`) add as built: activating changes only which of the seat's tools the phase is offered, and a pair a caller wrapped bare reached the bridge unannotated, where a person's stop refused a stopped run's discovery as a write it could not classify. It hands the extension judge the turn's fence token (`extension.Request.Boundary`), so the judge can rekey the task's fences onto a token of its own call, and writes the judge's verdict back into the conversation only through `extension.Nudge`, which defuses the judge's reason under that same turn token — a reason is a model's words about other people's words, and spliced in raw it could close a fence the seat reads. A person's NOTES reach a phase through ONE SOURCE (`SteerSource`, `Config.Steer`): the first segment's box, or the run's record a resumed segment reads — taken at a round of a host phase, PEEKED for a run's brief (`Brief`), whose launch records them read and publishes them delivered once it has launched (`Launched.LaunchID`), and given back when the launch fails BEFORE ITS WRITE (`Return`) — a launch that fails after it names the job it opened, and the record's ending reports them; a resumed segment opens with every note the record says the turn read (`Resume.Steered`), and the execute record lists its round's reads at round 1 with the kind of step — every job's of the round, the asking job's included where an answer carried the run on, as it lists that job's calls (`runReads`) Three kinds of round are CARRIED ON rather than collected: one a person's answer drives (`Asked`), one lost with its host (`Lost`), and one refused on a sign-in replaced while it ran (`Rotated`, once). A seat's EXECUTOR LISTS NO TOOL SKILL: each launch hands its harness the skills its phase matches as the harness's own (`handSkills`, `AgentRunRequest.Skills`), named `crewlet:<name>` from the key (`nativeNames`: lowercase, every run of anything but a letter or digit one hyphen, collisions told apart in key order), described by the summary and ending with a note for a required one, with the body `load_tool_skill` answers; its harness reports each load, which the bridge records as the run's `load_tool_skill` call, so the guard, the page's reads and every rebuild read one kind of load. The names are on the parked state (`execstate.State.NativeSkills`), which every rebuild hands the guard and every reopened bridge session reads a reported load by. EVERY LAUNCH ASKS WHICH SESSION IT CONTINUES (`continued.go`; `SessionProber`, asked before the briefs are written, on a turn's first launch too). A RELAUNCH CONTINUES THE SESSION OF THE JOB IT FOLLOWS where its launcher says it can: its brief is the session's next message (`keptSession`: what carries it on — a send-back's `prompts.BuildContinuedRound`, the answer, the loss, the sign-in — that it may end mid-call, every call the session had not been answered — every call the round's log took after the capture's save point (`SessionBasis.Through`, read against `BridgedCall.Appended`, never a call's place, so a call in flight at the read is told whatever the log dropped below it; one with no number is after every save point), rendered as the prior-work ledger renders a round and held to its budgets (`ledger.Format`, fitted as `priorWork` fits it) — then how many more it took after the save and dropped from its middle, exact where every call is numbered (`droppedAfterSave`: the appends past the point less the listed calls numbered past it, a listed call with no number never taken off, so a log an older build appended to may over-count, held to the round's dropped calls, and never under-counts), with the round's tally (`prompts.CalledAfter`, `ledger.FormatElided`) — every note the turn read after its `NoteCursor` (`steer.Reading.Order`, a read this segment made not yet numbered) and then the fresh ones), in the box it was last worked in and in any other (`prompts.BoxReplaced`), the fresh brief beside both — built, but for its lead (`keptBrief.led`), before the relaunch asks the seat's budget for the last time, since telling the calls after the save can call the seat's auxiliary model, while the lead of a round a person's answer carries on says what the call they approved returned, which is made only after that check; and the launch's context with it (`Continuation.ContextTokens`), for the floor of a run continued in its own box. A TURN'S FIRST LAUNCH, and a relaunch of a turn that has kept nothing, CONTINUES THE SESSION ITS CONVERSATION'S LAST TURN LEFT where its launcher answers one (`SessionBasis.Base`, `baseSession`): in a box of its own, its brief `prompts.BuildNextTurn`'s lead — where this turn begins, what a new box changes, and, where the base's turn's end said it went on past its session, where the session ends instead, or, where it was lost, that the session may not hold its last (`BaseBasis.WentOn`, `Lost`, `CapturedAt`) — then the launch's own fresh brief or reseed whole, which tells how the conversation's earlier turns ended (`Config.Endings`, frozen on the park as `execstate.Frozen.Endings`). A FRESH BRIEF NAMES THE KEPT SESSION ITS LAUNCH DOES NOT CONTINUE (`namingKeptSession`, `prompts.KeptSession`, appended as a section of its own, `prompts.KeyKeptSession`, by `prompts.Prompt.Then` after a base continuation has taken the brief whole): the session the probe read (`SessionBasis.KeptTurn`, the turn's own where a capture of it is kept, else the conversation's head the turn read, continued or not — on a relaunch only where the turn's row was read holding it, `sandbox.ContinuedSession.KeptTurn`), and to read it with `read_session` — only where the run's surface carries that tool, since a run that starts a session of its own cannot otherwise know one it could read is there — on every relaunch, a round lost a second time included, whose probe is asked for that alone; NEVER WHY it is not continued, which the probe words for the log and which quotes what said no, a store's error or what a box printed. THE GUARD FOLLOWS THE LAUNCH (`sessionDecided`, `AgentRunRequest.Decided`): the surface is built with an empty guard, and once the launch has its box and before the run starts it is armed for the session the run takes up (`skills.Guard.Replace`) — the launch state of the job it follows and that job's own loads (`ownCalls`: past `execstate.State.BridgeFrom`, a place in the order the bridge admitted calls, and none the log took after the capture's save point, by the test the calls after it are told by), or nothing for a session of its own or for the one the conversation's last turn left — and the brief the launch handed is published as the phase's opening frame (`emitter.prompted`). Every rebuild replays only its job's own loads (`rebuiltSurface`). |
| `agent/runner/steersourcetest` | The ONE contract suite every `runner.SteerSource` runs (`queuetest`'s idiom): the first segment's box (`steer.Box`, run from `agent/steer`) and the record of the executor a resumed segment reads (`internal/engine`'s source over the run's record, run from there) — two homes of a turn's notes the runner reads alike. The shared promises only: a waiting note is taken once, by one take, however many race for it; `Waiting` reports a note WITHOUT TAKING IT and never waits on a store, since the tool loop asks it under its dispatcher's lock; and a brief's notes are never lost and never reported twice — handed back after a launch that failed before its write, and taken again by the next reader; or, where the launch had written them read by a job that never ran, or another node's ending reached the record first, recorded expired exactly once, by the record's ending alone. A source with no record to write a brief on, or no store to stall, leaves out only the part of a case that needs one (a return, never a skip `internal/skipgate` would refuse); the box's bounds and the record's seals and fences stay in their own packages' suites |
| `agent/structured` | How a phase gives a typed answer: it CALLS A TOOL rather than writing prose the engine parses, so the ordinary tool loop carries the answer out and nothing needs a side channel. Three rules travel with the shape — a rejected submission goes back to the model (the one failure a model reliably fixes), the last write wins (a second submission is a correction), and an absent submission is not a value (every rescue path turns on telling "decided this" from "nothing decided anything"). A submission tool is SAFE FOR CONCURRENT CALLS, because a harness may make a response's calls at once and a bridged box's calls arrive on their own requests. The decoder belongs to the caller, and `Remarshal` — the one mapping from arguments to a typed payload, which `delegate` decodes through too — REFUSES a field the payload does not have, at any depth and by name: decoded the obvious way it was DROPPED, so a reviewer's misspelt `completed_work` never told the next round what had already landed, and a delegated task's `afer` ran at once on input it was told to wait for |
| `agent/phase` | The per-phase vocabulary: which phase is running, which model it runs on, and what a turn concluded. `execute` names the phase although it now decides as well as acts: deciding is part of the seat doing its own work, which is what every dashboard and rollup that reads the value means by it. Which entries a seat's phase runs on is ONE resolution (`Resolve`), and `ResolveWithSource` is the same walk also saying which level decided it (`seat`, `executor`, `default-entry`, `first-entry`), so a page that shows where a job lands reads the engine's answer rather than a copy of its precedence |
| `agent/toolloop` | One phase's model-and-tools conversation, and every rule a call is held to — THE HARNESS DRIVES THE ROUNDS; THE LOOP HOLDS THE PHASE (ADR-0049). Every model call is a harness running its own loop, so `Run` starts HARNESS RUNS of the phase's provider, each served the phase's tools by a DISPATCHER (`dispatcher.go`, the `llm.ToolHost`; each run's session hands its calls to a view bound to that run, `runCalls`, so a call is the run's that made it and a run already released refuses one) that decides each call as it arrives: the grant and the skill guard (the `Surface`), the fence before every run and before and after every call, each request charged as the harness's record shows it and a full window asked about only where the harness would ask its model again (never as a call is admitted, so a submission in the request that filled it still finishes the phase), the round cap (a round is one model request; the last allowed round's answers are WITHHELD and the run ends `exhausted`), a terminator or a call the surface marks detached (`Detacher`, which only the Dashboard Assistant's surface implements) run ALONE after its response's other calls — waiting only for calls the harness's declared `Concurrency` could be making beside it, since a harness that makes them in turn sends none while one is held — a call near the harness's own tool timeout answered "still running" so the run ends and the next one is handed the result, a person's note ending the run once its response's calls are answered so the NEXT run reads it as a USER message (never inside a tool result, which any tool's output could imitate), an activation on a harness that does not re-list ending the run, a panic cutting the phase, unparsed arguments answered and never run on `{}` (`UnparsedArguments`, exported so the bridge answers in the same words), and a call named other than the model asked — Hermes rewrites names — refused. Calls run under the PHASE's context, never the MCP request's, and the surface fixes each call's place in the run's call log AT ADMISSION (`Surface.Admit`), because a harness's calls return in whatever order their tools finish. Once a run is ending, every answer the harness would act on is withheld, so it makes no request it would be billed for. The FOLD (`fold.go`) turns each run back into the record the loop kept when it drove each round itself — assistant messages with their calls, tool results, `Execution`s with `CallID`, `Narration`, `Round`s — plus one `Invocation` per harness run (`end`, `cap`, `stopped`, `failed`) and a LIST of `Running` calls, so nothing downstream tells the two apart except by the runs it lists; a harness whose record shows no requests counts as one round per run. Between runs it does what only the loop can: a note, a corrective (a phase that finishes by a call is ASKED AGAIN when a run ends without it, `TerminateAfter`), a call's result the run ended before. And its CLOCK — every request and every tool call is timed here — and the `Suspend` primitive the Dashboard Assistant parks a turn on a proposal through (`Config.AllowSuspend`, which no seat phase sets). Every call is told its round's MODEL beside its round (`CallModel`, set by ONE setter, `WithCallModel`: here, by the dispatcher, from the round's own model — the completion's report, else the provider's identity, the precedence `Round.Model` records — and by the MCP bridge for a call a box's harness made), so a seat's code write names on its push the model that made it. Every phase the ENGINE drives on this host is this loop — the reviewer, a delegated worker, the onboarding pass, the assistant's quick mode — and a seat's executor is NOT: it is its harness's own run in a box, reaching the seat's tools over the bridge one call at a time (`api/mcpbridge`), whose record the runner reads back from the bridge's call log |

INSIDE AN EXECUTOR, which has no round of the engine's to open, it is read in the run's brief and at the harness's own boundaries between its steps (below) — at a point where every call has its answer either way, so a note can never split a call from its answer; the engine never folds one into a tool's result any tool's output could imitate (where a harness then places a hook's context is its own — on some models Claude Code appends it to the end of the last tool result — so a run's standing instruction tells a note by its headings, never by where it sits: `sandbox`), and never into the system prompt a provider caches on. The reviewer and every phase of the engine's own loop read notes; a worker, the onboarding pass and the judge do not. A turn whose executor is out keeps its notes NOT IN A BOX BUT ON THE RUN'S RECORD (internal/engine, runsteer.go, ADR-0067): the box is the first segment's only, until the launch hands what it holds over IN THE WRITE THAT CREATES THE RECORD (`Box.HandOver`'s notes ride it, waiting, ahead of any note filed there directly; `Box.Reopen` gives them back to a launch that failed before the write, and a launch that fails after it leaves them to the record's ending), and from there a note is read in a run's brief (`Box.Brief`, `Return` for a launch that failed before its write), between the run's steps through its bridge, or by the review — so the SOURCE a runner reads (`runner.SteerSource`) is a box or the record, never both. A read note is CARRIED into every later phase of the turn — from the run's record, which holds every read, when a segment resumes it — or the reviewer grades against the task the person corrected. A turn takes at most `MaxTurnNotes` (10) notes in all, answered `spent` past that, beside the five that may wait (`MaxPendingNotes`); an accepted note answers WHEN it is read (`Reads`: `next_step`, or `after_answer` for a run parked on a question). `Record` is the ONE constructor of `agent_turn_steered`, which every publisher calls — the runner, a run's bridge inbox and an ending — with the kind of step that read a note (`types.SteerBoundary`) and the run's job. The note is scattered on the queue's ephemeral verb, SIGNED and bound to one request on `signedask`'s `seat.steer` channel — the running node offers it as the person it names on the asking node's decision, so a note the fleet did not sign reaches no turn and an answer the asker cannot verify is no answer — and only the node running the turn answers — it remembers the last 256 turns it ended so a note that raced the end is `closed` rather than silence — and a retry of one request is one note, because the note's id IS the call's operation — the request's `Idempotency-Key` as `internal/api/opkey` scoped it to its principal — so an MCP call, which names none, is a new note every time. What became of it is `agent_turn_steered`: `delivered` where it was read, by the node whose step read it, or `expired` — by the node that closed the box, or that finished the run's ending — when the turn ended first. WHO MAY STEER is decided on the turn's SEAT — its lead, or `admin` — which a turn whose run is out names on its record under a SEALED ANCHOR, read by the asking node itself with no scatter; before that the node a request reached cannot know that seat until the running node says: `admin` admits at once and a caller who leads nobody is refused at once, while anybody else's call first sends a PROBE that offers nothing (one nobody answers is `unavailable`) and is decided again on the seat it names before the note is offered; the sender travels as `iam.ActorFor`'s author, kind and credential, never as a second bound-seat field beside them that could name somebody else |
| `agent/execstate` | The wire format for a turn PARKED on its executor's run. The run is detached in a box and outlives the process, so the turn is re-entered when the run is collected — after a restart, possibly on another node, possibly days later once a person answers its question — and what the rest of the turn needs is serialized into the pending-run row rather than parked in a goroutine. There is NO CONVERSATION in it (version 4): the run's own session holds its transcript, in its box, so what is kept is the turn's bookkeeping — the surface the run was offered, the rounds closed before it, what the turn was asked and by whom, what it wrote and owes — and the context the turn fetched once at its start, which every later launch of the turn is built from: the prefetched blocks and how the conversation's earlier turns ended (`Frozen.Endings`, which took the ledger's prior-turns block's place within version 4, a field every reader defaults going as one may come). The sandbox coordinator carries it back without ever decoding it. Evolution is additive WITHIN a version and a reshape takes a new number, never a reused one. Once a TAG has shipped a version, the build that replaces it carries a reader for it for as long as rows of it can be parked: nothing rewrites a parked row, and the layer holding the blob cannot decode it. A version this build does not read — 1 to 3 included, which no tag ever shipped, 3 being the parked engine conversation images of main wrote and a number never reused — is refused loudly and the row left for a node that can `NativeSkills` is the key of each skill the run's harness was handed as its own, by the name it lists it under: an added field a reader defaults, so no new version. | `agent/extension` | The round-cap extension judge: when a phase runs out of tool rounds, a cheap model says whether it is progressing or thrashing, and the engine grants more or falls through to the rescue path. The judge reads the turn's ask with its fences MOVED off the turn's token onto one minted for its call (`Request.Boundary`, `provenance.Rekey`) beside the standing sentence, and the reason it gives is defused under the turn's token in the `Nudge` the seat reads, because a judge echoes what it read |
| `agent/subagent` | `delegate`: the short-lived WORKERS an executor hands work to. A worker is a LEAF — it delegates nothing further and contacts no colleague — which is the only thing bounding the depth of the construct, so there is no depth counter anywhere. One call is a GRAPH: `after` makes a task wait for others and receive their submitted fields, run in topological waves under one barrier each, because a wave boundary is checkable where a per-task readiness queue's deadlocks are not. Three rules are enforced in code because a prompt is only a request: the grant is a security boundary (a config template widens nothing — every name still passes the same filter), one budget slice covers a whole call however many tasks it has, and an absent submission is `no_result` with the worker's prose rather than an answer the engine invented Each worker is a tool loop like any phase — its model a harness running its own loop over the worker's slice of tools, served from the same tool-session host, which a config without one is refused for before any task runs — and a worker's model call on its parent's entry may run in the parent run's slot, when the entry has no free one, rather than wait for a slot only that run could free. | `agent/inbox` | What wakes a seat, and what it must not be woken by twice. `ledgered` is the completion side |

The same budgets (`Format`: the value limit and the read cap) hold the calls a relaunch that continues a kept session is told it made after the session's save (`agent/runner`'s `calledAfter`). ACROSS TURNS IS NOT ITS: a conversation's next turn continues the session its last turn left and is told how the earlier turns ended from the executor log (`executordomain`, rendered by `agent/prompts`), so a conversation has one history — its transcript — rather than a second account kept beside it. | `agent/prompts` | The prompt text, and one builder per phase — and EVERY BUILDER RETURNS ITS OUTLINE BESIDE ITS TEXT (`outline.go`): the parts it appended, each keyed, titled, measured and marked headed or not, because only the frame that appended a part knows where content quoting its own headings begins and ends. Prompt text is behaviour, changed deliberately with its tests and docs. The executor's two code sections, `code_history` (read on the server, never from a clone, and a change's diff, its findings and what changed since a review with `code_get_change`) and `code_writes` (a small change committed on the server, anything to build or test in a checkout), are each gated on EVERY tool its claims rest on (`CodeHistoryTools`, `CodeWriteTools`), which internal/agent/builtin's tests hold to the code tools it registers; `code_history` adds that a repository the executor's run is given on Gitlet is cloned blobless — so its history is for building, not for answering questions. A schedule's conversation is told in its own words, in the block, in the lead and in the kept-session notice alike (`ConversationEndings.Fires`, `NextTurn.Fire`, `KeptSession`'s `fire`): its earlier fires, and a new fire that the schedule firing again woke. A SECTION APPENDED TO A BUILT PROMPT (`Prompt.Then`) tiles it as a builder's last part would, the separator staying with the section before it: how a launch's fresh brief names the kept session it does not continue (`KeptSession`, keyed `KeyKeptSession`) after a base's continuation has taken the brief whole. |

its request id is the call's operation (`opIDFor`), so the same call again is the same request the committer's ledger collapses (`CodeWriter.Expunge`, the estate's `code.expunge`); answered `{request, position, maintainer, holds{gitlet_nodes, backups_before, store_until}}`, the maintainer and the Gitlet nodes read through `CodeDeps.Placement` (the engine's router, by `cache.PlacementCharge`), a placement it cannot read SAID (`unplaced`) beside a request recorded all the same; destructive and idempotent; never offered to a seat. `code_import_repo` (codeimport.go, the last of `CodeWrites` as `ImportWrites`) is a PERSON'S create of a project filled from a repository at another host — a lifecycle create carrying `LifecycleRequest.Import`, or with `mirror` the settings' `MirrorFrom` and no import beside it (a pull mirror imports from its own source) — which the repository's home fetches (code/mirror): authz `{ClassApp gitlet, humanOnly, RecencyAny}` (U49 a: an import dials another host, so never an agent's, and the deciding data node refuses a seat's create carrying either again), a token bound to nobody refused `code.UnboundDetail`; `credential` is a variable's NAME in UPPER CASE, made the `${NAME}` the record carries — upper case because a forge's token (`ghp_…`) is a valid reference name, and taken as one it would be recorded on the settings; the repository's id derived from the call's operation as `code_create_repo`'s is, so the same call again is the same create; answered as a create (`codeRepoWrite.answer`), the repository `importing`; idempotent, not destructive; never offered to a seat. CHATLET is the fourth domain here (`chat.go`, `chatoperator.go`): nine tools a seat holds and seven only a person makes, over ONE `ChatDeps` seam the estate router's `Chat`/`ChatSearch` satisfy (asserted at compile time). A room is said and READ as a seat, so an actor that names none is refused before any read; an edit's and a delete's authority is decided after reading WHOSE WORDS the message is (`remarkAuthority`: admin on the unread remark is MODERATION, carried to the store as `chatlet.MessageAuthority`), and an archive after reading the stored room (`chat.channel.archive`, its unit carried as a precondition). EVERY KEYED WRITE — a page's and a chat gesture's — takes its key from ONE derivation (`callOpKey`): in a turn the turn's seed, its instant, the tool, the arguments' digest and the repeat count among the tool's FAMILY (`chatlet.CallFamily`, so a join after a leave is a new join); outside one the key the transport carried; there is no per-domain copy. EVERY DOMAIN A SURFACE WRITES IS DECLARED ONCE (`nativeDomains`, writerclass.go): the refusal class and the sentence its writer's errors get and the arguments that name its objects, which the person's write surface reads for its tool-less verbs (`WriterClass`, `ObjectArgs`), held both ways to `estate.SurfaceWriteDomains` — so never the executor log, whose writes are the engine's own record of its runs and no surface's (the estate's engine-originated class), and whose writer no file here may name. WHICH OF ITS TOOLS HAND A MODEL SOMEBODY ELSE'S WORDS IS DERIVED, never listed: the plain encoder (`jsonAnswer`) refuses an answer holding a field a record declares somebody's words (`provenance.FieldTag`), a `foreignRead` refuses one it did not fence or name the writers of, and a sweep calls every tool both surfaces register against stores whose every declared field and every stored body spells a forged closer, holding each answer to the fence's property and the set of tools whose answers carry those words to `handsOverWords` in both directions — the tracker's listings, the inbox, the activity feed, a knowledge answer's sources and a parked run's question were each handed over bare before it. THE CATALOGUE (`catalogue.go`) files every built-in a seat is offered, and the runner's discovery pair, on one of ten GROUPS — the code tools on `code`, `fleet_health` and `code_status`, which read the deployment's health rather than one repository's, on `health` — with the GATE its authority row asks (twelve words, from `everybody` to `artifact_owner`, among them `health_tools`, named after the seat grant the health tools' rows decide an agent by), because holding a tool is not being allowed to call it and a reader auditing what an agent holds needs both. The gate is DECLARED rather than read off `authz.ClassOf`, which is exported for walks and not for a caller to branch on: it names and never decides, and a walk holds every declared gate to its row's class, app and artifact role both ways (a personal verb that takes no name reads as its app, its object being the caller), so a row that changes turns the walk red until the catalogue agrees. `GET /tools`, the `tools` push and `mcp_servers_status`'s `builtin` shelves carry both, on the one row shape `queries.CatalogueRow` builds. A SEAT'S OWN EXECUTOR SESSIONS (`sessions.go`, ADR-0073) are two tools on the `memory` shelf: `list_sessions`, the seat's rows newest begun first (ten a page and at most ten — the most whose page, every field of every row at its bound, fits one 64 KiB tool answer: 5,994 bytes a row at its worst, so an eleventh does not, which its test measures both ways — each row's words cut to 300 bytes and marked `this_turn` and `this_conversation` off the bridged turn, and carrying, as a person's read surface does, whether its session is in progress, with the engine's sentence for one, unfenced since it quotes nobody, and the domain's note on a session its turn went on past, fenced as the row's words are: `in_progress`, `in_progress_note` and `kept_note`), or with `query` a search of their words answered where the rows are, whose page says how many sessions it searched and never that nothing matches past them — nor among them where the copy that answered could not read every record, which it says in words (`incompleteSessions`, `incompleteSearch`) beside the flag; and `read_session`, a page of one session's transcript through `executorread` held to a seat's bounds and its one slot, narrowed by `kinds` or `match` (each hit the window of its redacted text around the first word it shows, with `text_from` and a cursor of its own; every part the read could not read handed out whatever the filter, the page's note saying it could not search those), trimmed by its encoded size to one tool answer (`fitLabelled`, its cursor naming the first entry left out) and bounded at `SessionReadWithin` (two minutes), a session whose object failed and whose row the log did not read again said apart from a store that did not answer (`executorread.ErrKeptUnknown`). NEITHER TAKES A SEAT: each reads the seat of the turn its call is bound to, so another seat's turn is answered as one nobody has; both are reads (`annotationsFor`), their rows an agent seat's own verbs of the self class, offered on no person's surface and never to the reviewer; every word is fenced by `provenance.ExecutorSession` through the one door `sessionLabel`, an entry naming the seat whose run kept it, the row's words nobody. A read holds nothing, and a session released while it is read is said as released. Registered where `Deps.Sessions` holds all three of its parts, which the engine hands over only where the epoch keeps sessions, on a node with the router and an object store; and EVERY CALL ASKS THE SWITCH of the revision its node runs (`SessionDeps.Keeps`), refusing as forbidden once that keeps no session, so a launch that pinned an earlier revision is stopped at its next call, not at its end. A COLLEAGUE'S ASK CARRIES WHOEVER THE ASKING TURN WORKS FOR (`workingForOf`, from the call's bound ceiling, never from the ask's arguments: `types.WorkingFor` on the ask and on the answer back), and the woken turn reads it before anything else (`workingForCeiling`: a seat composed again on its node, a credential narrowed again and never widened, a stranger kept), so a chain of asks never widens (ADR-0109's amendment). |
| `agent/colleague` | Resolving a free-text query to a seat — the lookup before an A2A ask, a chat mention or a page mention. A model types what it remembers, so the answer is either one seat or an honest list of who it might be, NEVER a guess. Four tiers, earlier ones short-circuiting later, so a query that is exactly somebody's handle is never fuzzy-matched against everybody else |
| `agent/turnctx` | What a turn IS, carried as an explicit argument rather than ambient state. A turn has at least five values that want to travel ambiently, and a goroutine SHARES whatever context it captured — forever, including after the turn that created it finished — so what would elsewhere merely obscure a dependency is a live data race here. A turn's LOOKUPS (`Lookups`) hold what it resolved by name once — a code tool's repository — and facts those lookups established that a later call builds on (how far the refs it resolved on a repository had moved, taken with `LoadOrStore` so callers racing to be first share one value), keyed like a context by its consumer's own type, shared by every Turn derived from it and empty again on a resumed segment; they authorize nothing, since the node answering each later read judges the asker again. A turn's HOLDS (`Holds`) are what Gitlet could delete from under it on nobody's request — the scratch repositories it named and the seats' branches it read, wrote or launched on, by opaque keys — taken before each request, a call's keys in ONE write to the turn's run row (`Take` takes them together, so a comparison of two seats' branches is one compare-and-set, not two), kept in memory and on the turn's run row once it has one; beside the set they mark which keys THIS PROCESS has CONFIRMED (`Confirm`, M3-decisions M3-O65) — in memory only, never on the row, because the row carries keys taken unconfirmed too, so a resumed turn confirms again. A seat's PRINCIPAL is derived by ONE function from the organization and the seat (`SeatPrincipal`), which `Principal` calls for a turn, so the engine decides what a seat is offered as the very principal its calls are decided as. A turn's HOLDS (`Holds`, M3-O61) are the code repositories it has named, taken BEFORE each request about one goes out and never released while the turn is unended, so Gitlet's scratch expiry spares them: at most `MaxHolds` (1024) a turn, written first to the turn's run row where it has one (`Attach`'s writer) and only then held, and a `Seal` around a launch makes a hold taken meanwhile wait for the row, so no hold is ever only in memory while the turn lives on a row. Its `CallLog` counts a call's repeats (`Ordinal`, which every derived operation id carries), and a resumed run SEEDS it BY IDENTITY (`SeededCall.Digest`, the digest the run's log admitted the call under), never by what a record kept of the arguments, which a run's log and a parked turn keep in part; a call whose identity a record could not keep, or withholds (a held call's, whose arguments ride sealed), is seeded as one matching no other (`SeededCall.Unknown`, `SeedUnknown`), so a seed can only over-count, which is a fresh operation, and never under-count, which would answer a new write with an earlier one's id — provided the record holds every call the log did: an admitted call's OWN WORK (a `delegate`'s workers, on forks of its fork) is handed back by `CallLog.Own` for the record to keep beside it. |

WHICH CLASS IS ONE RULE for every domain (the `Refusal` doc in `mcp`), by what the refusal is ABOUT and what would make the same request land: the request itself (an argument outside its grammar, a value past a limit of its own, an argument naming ANOTHER object that cannot take part (a parent in the trash)) is `invalid`; the object the call is about (or the container it writes into) absent is `not_found`; that object in a STATE that refuses the gesture until somebody changes it (a room or a project archived, an item frozen in the trash, an artifact in the trash, its own contents at their cap (a message's emoji, a project's tags, a task's watchers or checklists, a person's pins, every label an artifact keeps in use)) is `conflict`, as a lost race is; and a limit the vocabulary names a class for (`quota_exceeded`, `inbox_full`, `reassignment_budget`, `notes_full`, `notes_spent`, `budget_exhausted`) is that class. `agent/builtin`'s `TestEveryDomainRefusalIsClassed` holds every sentinel each native domain declares to the MEANING its row states and the class that meaning takes, on the domains' table and on each domain's own tools alike, and the meaning to the sentinel's own NAME where the name says one (a …Taken, …Clash or …Exists is a collision and every collision is named so; Each MCP tool also carries what its server is FOR (`Entry.ServerDescription`), stamped at registration from what the registry was told (`DescribeServers`, from each apply's revision, carried by `Clone`) and kept ON THE ENTRY so every cut of a snapshot, a worker's grant rebuilt entry by entry included, keeps it; `Snapshot.Discoverable` prints it beside the server's name. | `tools/argval` | How a first-party tool READS ONE ARGUMENT a model sent: ONE READER PER DECLARED TYPE, which both decides whether a value is one and returns the value read (ADR-0059) — a string takes a number or a boolean as the model wrote it, a list of strings one string or a comma-separated one, an integer and a number a value or a decimal text that spells one exactly (`Whole`, `Number`), a boolean only true or false, and a closed set its member trimmed and without regard to case (`Choice`). The surface's check of a call against its schema calls it to decide and the builtin tools' helpers call the same reader to read, so a value the check admits is read as exactly what it spells: with a reader each, a set written as `"GP-12"` passed the check as a list and the tool read no list, and `"1e3"` passed as an integer and the tool read 1. A property test holds the check and every helper to the exact value over a corpus of awkward spellings. A LEAF over the standard library |
| `tools/toolargs` | A tool call's ARGUMENTS, from the transport that carried them to the one form every step of the call reads (ADR-0059). `Decode` is the ONE DECODE every transport into a tool shares — the HTTP write surface, the act transport, the operator's MCP and a harness's tool session: nothing at all (empty, whitespace or `null`) is a call with no arguments, and anything else is EXACTLY ONE JSON object, read THROUGH json.Number, so an integer past 2^53 reaches the tool as the digits it was sent as, and a second value after it is refused rather than dropped in silence. `Of` makes the CANONICAL FORM ONCE, AT THE ENTRY, a closed set's member as its set spells it (`" Draft"` is `"draft"`), and `Args`, a type only `Of` makes, is what every step after it requires: the run's call log and the repeat count an operation id carries, the skill guard, the refusal-loop target, the check, the tool, the ledger, logging and metrics. | `modelnote` | The sentence a tool call answered a MODEL with (a refusal's, or the note on a successful call's arguments, ADR-0059), carried IN PROCESS ONLY, from the route that answered it to an in-process caller whose own model made the request: the Dashboard Assistant executing a change its person approved (ADR-0060). | `mcp` | MCP client and child supervision. A stdio server is a process TREE, not a process, and its environment is `hostbox`'s allowlist, the engine user's HOME and XDG directories, and what its `env:` and the seat's `mcp_env` declare, NEVER the engine's own: a server that reads anything else declares it, with a `${VAR}` reference to pass the host's value through, and lists the key under the server's `optional_keys` where a host may set none. A server whose `command` is `docker` or `podman` IS the runtime's CLI and gets `hostbox.ContainerRuntime`, the runtime's own settings beside the host user's locations, because a rootless runtime without its `DOCKER_HOST` dials the system socket. The package doc says why the obvious `os.Environ()` is wrong. Every server a bridge runs is SUPERVISED until it is stopped: the engine makes the child's one Wait itself rather than the SDK's transport, and watches the transport's read too, so a death (or a session that ended while its process lives on) is an event and not a broken pipe found by the next call. A bridge's `Health` says since when, how many restarts, why it is down, its last failure kept after it is back and when it last answered. `Bridge.RestartBefore` restarts what began before an instant (a serving session ended for a fresh one at once, a down server tried now, its schedule started again), so a request read twice or late restarts nothing more; a requested restart is logged as requested and is no failure. A TEST (`test.go`, `Test`) brings up a connection of its own exactly as `connect` does, walks its stages (address, resolve, connect, tls, discover, list for a remote server; launch, discover, list for a local one), each timed through the standard library's trace hooks on a transport clone of the test's own, lists the tools as the engine would offer them and closes it, NEVER CALLING A TOOL; its sentences withhold every header and variable value the spec carries and write the address through `redact.URL`. `CheckAddress` (`addresscheck.go`) tests an address with nothing configured and, on a Bearer challenge, reads its RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 metadata, every address the server names on another origin fetched only through `httpx.Guarded`, over https, following no redirect. A REMOTE CONNECTION FOLLOWS A REDIRECT WITHIN ITS CONFIGURED ORIGIN ALONE (`http.go`), and sets the configured headers only on a request to that origin. `StartingLevel` is the level a tool starts at where its entry sets none and no default (read-only `allow`, every other `approve`, an unannotated tool included), which every filed `Tool` carries resolved (`Definition.Level`). A TOOL'S LEVEL IS DECIDED WHERE IT IS FILED (`levels.go`, `Spec.Levels`, by the server's own name, with a default for every tool no level names): a blocked tool is never built as a `Tool` but kept as a `Definition`, which nothing can call (`Bridge.BlockedTools`), so no catalogue holds it and every reader of a seat's surface (the relay, the bridge, the discovery tools) agrees it is not there; a tool at `approve` is filed, marked on every registry entry (`tools.Entry.NeedsApproval`), and never called through a catalogue until a person answers (ADR-0077). A tool's `Parts` name each part of its definition apart, and `Tool.Unreviewed` asks the bridge's owner at each call whether the definition is the one its level was decided on (ADR-0078). there. A MOVEMENT IS IDENTIFIERS AND A COUNT — source, handle, unread delta, subject, reason, five fields a test holds — never content, because it rides a socket frame to whoever watches the seat and content there would be a read path around the inbox question's authority. Its refusals are its own sentinels (`ErrInvalid`, `ErrFull`) with the sentence a person reads (`Sentence`); a domain's writer classes the invalid ones as its own. GITLET KEEPS ITS OWN: a person's code marks are `code_person_marks`, written by `marks` records on their own `person.<handle>` subject of the code log, never on Worklet's person record — a position counts on one stream. |

THE RULE IS NOT "hash secrets with argon2id", it is SPEND COST WHERE AN ATTACKER HAS A SHORTCUT — a password came from a space small enough to grind, so it gets 64 MiB and t=3; a recovery code, a machine token and a reset link's secret are values this engine minted — `crypto/rand`, or for a first password link a MAC under the company's key, so a create's retry hands back the same link — so there is no dictionary and SHA-256 is the whole of it, and a token is presented on every request a pipeline makes. `p=1` is the parameter most often set wrong: parallelism makes ONE verification finish sooner and does nothing to an attacker already running every core they own, while costing the ability to serve concurrent sign-ins at all. `VerifyCap` is DERIVED as max(1, NumCPU/p) because each verification holds 64 MiB — uncapped, an unauthenticated caller turns the endpoint into an out-of-memory kill — and it bounds EVERY derivation through one path, a verification at the stored verifier's own cost as much as a hash: `Verify` used to call argon2 directly, so the cap bounded setting a password and nothing a stranger could send. THE CAP IS A PLAIN SEMAPHORE, first come first served, that every `Hash`, `Verify` and `Decoy` waits in on the REQUEST'S CONTEXT, so a waiter whose request went away leaves and nothing is derived for nobody — it was one queue with no bound and no context, so derivations ran for clients that had hung up; and it was then per-source turns, one slot per address served in turn, which bought a timing equalisation nothing asks for any more at the price of a scheduler of its own. `Rehash`, the one derivation nobody waits on, takes a slot only if one is free NOW and never one a freed slot hands to a waiter. GIT'S HASHFILE TRAILER IS ONE RULE (`hashfile.go`, ADR-0008): `HashTrailer` over the piece loop `HashPieces` is what both a layer's check and the cache's check, scrub and Verify hold a file's trailer by — the same layer files reach both, fetched and then kept — and what `crewlet gitlet export` holds the bundle it writes by, reading a file a piece at a time in a slot its caller's hold takes (`Pieces`: a Gitlet node's read lane, a piece of the cache's `CheckPieceBytes`) and checking its context before every read, so a check of the largest repository's root layer, some 2.6 GB, stops when its caller does and never holds a read slot for more than a piece; so every reader here, `CheckLayer` and `LayLayer` take a context and `Pieces`. `CheckLayer` holds a layer's three files to its row and the chain below it before any git process is handed them — each file exactly its section, the multi-pack-index's trailer the row's `LayerID` and its PNAM the row's `Packs`, the bitmap that index's with its tables fitting it, the commit-graph layer's BASE the GraphIDs of the rows below it and its filters version 2 — refusing `ErrBadLayer` naming the field, definite and never retried, while a failed read, a refused hold and an ended context are answered as they came; `LayLayer` states a row's byte fields from the files a build wrote by the same reading and holds them to each other and to the base the build was written over (its commit-graph layer's BASE exactly the base rows' GraphIDs, `CheckLayer`'s one comparison), so a build whose files no node would install is refused before a byte is stored, and the publisher has only its plan's packs left to compare. A layer's bytes, the three files back to back, are `LayerPartBytes` parts cut by ONE rule both ways (`layerPart`: a part's start in the layer and its runs in the files, by its index): `StoreLayer` uploads every part at once as `LayerContentType`, each under `UploadDeadline`, the first failure the answer and the parts stored the collector's, and `FetchLayerPart` lays one part read through the store's verified read (`LayerReader`, which `*objstore.Store` satisfies) back where it came from. Its COMMIT (`ExpungeCommit`, op id its own `CommitID`, never the begin's) retires exactly the repository's dropping packs into `code_packs_retired` and keeps a live RESCUE (`PackRescue`) of what a push landed between scan and begin revived; its ONE precondition is its expunge, open at its epoch — no ref, so nothing a push does starves it. A person's purge is a REQUEST (`OpExpungeRequest`, `ExpungeRequest`, a bound person's): it records `expunge_request` and its position and nothing else, a later one while it is open is recorded too and WIDENS it to its own id and position (it asks about more: a pack pushed between the two, what a ref dropped between them left), and it is SERVED — cleared — once no pack dates its CONTENT from before it (`requestServed`, one seek of `code_packs_content_idx`: at its own record for a repository with no pack, at a commit otherwise). WHAT A HOME FETCHED LANDS AS RECORDS OF THEIR OWN (`decide_remote.go`, `apply_remote.go`): an import's chunks (`import_chunk`, ONLY IN ITS TURN — `Seq` one past the row's `import_seq`, else `stale`) and its end (`import_done`, the status back to active, `import_error`, the source's HEAD as the default branch only where the declared one did not arrive), and a pull mirror's syncs (`mirror_sync`, refused `expunging` unrecorded against a moved `drop_epoch`, M6-D4; one of no pack and no command — its source found level, `MirrorSync.Current` — writes only `mirror_synced_at` and no push, as a pull mirror's import that landed whole sets it at its end, so a quiet mirror leaves the head of `mirrors_due`), each through the repository's one queue alone (`Committer.ProposeImport`/`ProposeMirrorSync`, estate `code.import`/`code.mirror_sync`), each command's old the row's tip or the whole record `stale`, and each landing as ONE PUSH through `landPushes` — a push row `via import` or `via mirror` by the engine's own account, its several packs the record's (`recordPacks`, kind `import`/`mirror`, so the row names no single pack), the ref drops and the changes it moves; `imports_due` (one walk of `code_repos_importing_idx`) and `mirrors_due` (push mirrors by id, then pull mirrors least recently synced first, on their two partial indexes) are the home's listings, and a home cuts each record to what it carries before it uploads a pack (`ImportProposal.Fitted`, `MirrorSyncProposal.Fitted`: at most `MaxImportRefs` refs and the most whose encoding fits `EntryRoom`, each pack measured as stored). A CHAIN (`ChainBuild`, `ChainEntry`, `ChainChange`/`ChainChangeOf`, `ChainCommit`, `ChainResult`; chain.go) is the home's in-process ask of its Gitlet node's builder for a run of queue entries merged in one scratch — never a record, so held to no record format — at most `MaxChainEntries` (64 = `MaxPushesPerRecord`, the most one landing names), its objects at most `MaxChainObjectBytes` uncompressed (16 MiB, what its pack measurably deflates and checks well inside `ChainPackDeadline`; host's BenchmarkBuildChain) and its pack so at most `MaxChainPackBytes` (twice that, by construction), each entry held besides to a merge_change's own pack bound, its git at most `ChainBuildDeadline` (its merges one `MergeBuildDeadline` together, the first entry all of it, and `ChainPackDeadline` for its pack, inside home's one-minute turn), NEVER REFUSED WHOLE — every refusal names the one entry it skips, and the entries its time or its objects' bound did not reach are left out of `ChainResult.Commits`, a prefix, for the next chain — each entry's author date its entry's instant (`QueueEntryID` keeps the enqueue's), `Validate` naming the field. A ONE-REPOSITORY CODE SEARCH is a git read (`GitSearch`, `search.go`: `SearchQuery` carries codeindex's query AS ITS PARTS — text, mode, case, paths, ref — never a compiled pattern, so the answering node builds the expression and its plan by the one grammar the asker validated with; `SearchAnswer`, `SearchHit`, `SearchVia` `index`/`grep`; `MaxSearchHits` 500, `MaxSearchLineBytes` 256, `MaxIndexedFileBytes` = `codeindex.MaxFileBytes`, `SearchBudget` the resolve budget), an estate request rather than a record, with the unready reason `index_building` (`UnreadyIndexBuilding`, passing no fill) |
| `chatlet` | Chatlet, the engine's own CHAT, and `statelog`'s NINTH domain — channels, unit rooms, direct conversations, threads, messages, edits, tombstoned deletes, reactions, retention, erase and the prune — on `CREWLET_CHAT_LOG`. It is the domain with TWO DISCIPLINES ON ONE STREAM, and that is the whole of what makes it different: a room's own state (topic, purpose, membership, archive, retention) arbitrates on the room's subject as the other domains do, while a MESSAGE is `PatternSequenced` on the room's MESSAGE subject — one subject per room rather than per message — because two people talking in one room are not racing for anything, so an expectation there would serialise the hottest subject in the company behind itself and answer `ErrConflict` on a message somebody typed. SEQUENCED AND NOT ADDITIVE, because a message does not commute with what lands just ahead of it: the APPLIER decides each message record at its position and writes a VERDICT for every one (`chat_verdicts`, replicated migration 0068 — `applied`, or `archived`, `not_member`, `gone`, `deleted`, `reactions_full`, or `repeated` for a second copy of an operation, which does nothing; an archive and a full message are each refused as the STATE of what the gesture is about, `ErrArchived` and `ErrReactionsFull`, a conflict — kept the operation ledger's thirty days beside the highest position the prune has let go, `chat_verdicts_lost` (0070), because a pruned verdict and a record every node's gate dropped leave the same absence and the first is answered `unknown` and unvouched, never dropped), the writer reads it back before it answers and answers a refusal with the sentinel its own decision would have refused with (`Store.decided`), a retry the ledger answers reads its first copy's, and the change feed withholds the wake of a record this node refused while failing open where it has not decided one, so the company's wakes never wait on one node's applier; a rule a later build may change travels on the record (`MessagePost.MembersOnly`, `Reaction.Cap`) and the applier decides only the facts at its position. A message's SCOPE is its CHANNEL'S and there is no per-message term in the alphabet: the applier mints `channel_seq` from log order, which is deterministic only while a deferred record BLOCKS its channel (ADR-0046). A keyed gesture's operation id is derived from the caller's key on the actor (`Actor.OpKey`) through `statelog.KeyedOpID` over what the gesture ASKS, never what it resolved to, and a message's id IS its operation's. A SPEAKER IS A SEAT: a credential acting as itself (`AuthorOperator`) speaks in no room and reads none, and may only erase, prune and set a room's retention, which reach past membership without reading. The STORE judges values, never authority: a moderator's delete arrives as `MessageAuthority{Moderate}` and an archive as `ChannelAuthority`, decided by the asking node's authz and judged against the stored row. A DM's identity is DERIVED from the sorted handles in it. WHO A MESSAGE WAKES is `recipients.go`, one function set the decide and the parser both call — a PURE `Candidates` over the record and an impure `Route` over the live roster — and PEOPLE ARE NEVER WOKEN. A PERSON IS NEVER ANSWERED BY SILENCE: a person's message in a named room that names no seat the company has (a person included) and reaches no agent wakes the room's ANSWERER, one seat, resolved at write time through the roster and carried on the record (a unit's lead, otherwise the room's most senior agent member by `Roster.Senior`), and a person's `@channel` is a request (`collective_request`, addressed) where an agent's is news (`collective`): two reasons rather than one read with its author, because whether a wake obliges an answer is the reason's alone. A ROOM IS NAMED AS PEOPLE WRITE IT by one rule (`RoomRef`: its id, or its name with or without the `#` before it), which a seat's tools and the API's room questions both read a typed room by, and the set of rooms a viewer may read, which scopes a search, carries each room's name and kind beside its id (`ReadableRoom`), read with the set, so a hit is shown under the name the room had where the search was allowed to read it. The names of every room a viewer may read are a read of their own (`RoomNames`), the named rooms alone and bounded at `MaxRoomNames`, every live room before an archived one: what a reader tells a room written in prose (`#e2e`) from a colour or an issue's number by. What is NOT here: read cursors, mutes and do-not-disturb, which are in `coord` because a cursor is one reader's attention nobody replays; and its search, a keyword index of its own in `search` (`ChatIndexer`) with no vectors at all, because chat is a keyword corpus only (ADR-0071). Its read types DECLARE the fields that hold somebody else's words (`untrusted:"fence"` or `untrusted:"name"`, `provenance.FieldTag`), which the agent's read tools may not answer unlabelled |
| `knowledge` | The backend-neutral seam the turn-start knowledge prefetch and the `search_knowledge` builtin both read through. Exactly ONE backend per company, because two would make "what do we already know about this" depend on which searcher was asked. A caller passes a seat, plain text and ancestor exclusions — never a CQL fragment, a space key or a project list — and search is BEST EFFORT: every failure path is an empty result, so a turn never dies because a wiki was slow — and a search that never ran says so (no mode served, none of the corpus covered), so "the knowledge base could not be searched" is never told as "nothing matched". | `providers/llm` | The model contract, sized to what a harness can be handed and can honestly report — EVERY `providers.llm` entry is one (`harness`), and the only other implementations are the chain and test doubles. A conversation in and an answer and its usage out, and, for a seat at work, the phase's tools beside the conversation as a `ToolHost` (`toolhost.go`): the backend serves it to its harness as ONE MCP server for the length of the call, tells it what the harness's own record shows of each model request (`Observe`, a `Turn` with its `TurnCall`s) and what each cost (`Spent` — per request while running, and the unreported remainder at the end on EVERY outcome), stops its harness when `Done` closes, and hands a fallback member what the phase already did (`Pending`) unless the phase is decided (`Halted`). NOTHING ELSE: no temperature, no output cap, no effort, no reasoning field, because no harness takes one per call, and a field no backend sends is a setting every caller believes it changed — a caller that needs a short answer says so in its prompt. | `providers/llm/chain` | The seat's model fallback: an `llm.Provider` over its entries, tried in order. A FATAL kind stops it too — a call the engine or its host cannot make (a prompt it cannot render, a harness it cannot start), which is the operator's to fix — and nothing else does: a harness that RAN and failed, however it failed, is its vendor's outage or its own crash, and the next member shares neither.
