| `sourcetree` | What is and is not THIS REPOSITORY'S TREE, for everything that reads its own files: the module root (`Root`) and a walk (`Walk`) that never enters VCS metadata, a NESTED CHECKOUT or a `node_modules`. `Root` is where every path a test takes out of its own package starts — a docs page, the examples, the schemas, the dashboard build, the directory `go list ./...` runs in — never a counted `../..`, which is a depth every copy had to get right for itself and one did not. The middle one is why it exists: this repository is developed with `isolation: worktree`, which puts full checkouts of it under `.claude/worktrees/`, and of twenty-one walks, each with its own idea of the tree, the only one that stepped over them did so by skipping every dot-directory — a name, not a rule — so the rest read those copies as this tree's, so the withdrawn-vocabulary gate failed on a clean tree by finding its own list in a nested copy, and a presence check passes on a stale one. A nested checkout is recognised by STRUCTURE — any directory below the start holding a `.git` entry of its own, file or directory, whether or not it resolves to a repository — never by the name `.claude`, which would miss a clone dropped anywhere else. That is DELIBERATELY BROADER than git's embedded-repository rule, which walks into a dangling gitfile or an empty `.git` and would stage what it finds there: a pruned worktree is still a copy of this tree at another commit, and broader is the safe direction for a guard, because git never tracks a `.git` path, so a fresh checkout — CI's — holds none and the walk there reads every committed file. Every other skip (static/, dist/, schema/, testdata) stays the guard's own decision, and reaches only what lies BELOW the start: `Walk` never hands its start to the callback, because the start's name is wherever the checkout lives, and a checkout at `../dist` was skipped whole by every gate that steps over dist/ — and each of those asserting an absence without counting what it read passed having read nothing. A start that is not a directory is an error for the same reason, since `filepath.WalkDir` does not follow a symbolic link at its start, and `Root` resolves its links so a checkout reached through one is still read. `gofiles` is the same rule for the formatter: `gofmt -l .` enters every nested checkout, so `make fmt` rewrote another worktree's files. The disk rather than `git ls-files`, because the compiler reads untracked files and a guard over the index passes a violation until the commit that tracks it. It is also where a gate learns which Go source it may SKIP without parsing: `Identifiers` skips a file spelling none of the identifiers a syntax-tree matcher compares — exact because an identifier has no escapes, and refused for anything that is not one. What a regular expression lets a gate skip is `regexlit`'s, not this package's: it moved out so that production code can read the same derivation, and production code does not import this package, which imports `testing`.`ModuleRoot` is `Root` for a value several gates of one binary load once. `TypeCheck` is THE MODULE'S ONE WAY FOR A GATE TO TYPE-CHECK ITS SOURCE with the standard library alone — `go/types` over the export data `go list -export -deps` answers, run by the toolchain that built the test (`CREWLET_GO`, or `GOROOT`'s) with its `-race` and `-tags`, so it reads what the run compiled — handing each package over after everything of the module it imports, only the packages its patterns name and its `Select` keeps; with `Tests`, each as its test binary compiles it: with its in-package test files, and its external test package against the package's TEST VARIANT (`p [p.test]`, which holds an `export_test.go`'s names) and against every package the binary compiles again (`q [p.test]`), each BUILT FROM SOURCE rather than compiled for export data — the in-package unit is `p [p.test]`, and every `q [p.test]` is a module package checked against it — so the export data it asks for is the plain packages' alone, from a second `go list` after a `-test` listing that compiles nothing (`-export -test` compiled every variant, external test package and test main: 169 s after a source change and 390 s cold for fixedwait's 52 packages on two cores). It was `words`' gate's private loader, lifted so that no gate writes a second copy; `decltype` is the other road, for a gate that cannot afford to build what the judged packages import |
| `sourcetree/decltype` | THE ONE WALK THAT TYPES A VALUE FROM THE DECLARATIONS IT REACHES, for every static gate that judges a value by what it IS rather than by its name — `statelog`'s stream-identity gate, `api/paced`'s pacing gate, `code/cache`'s writers gate, `api/auth`'s one-classifier gate, `code/host`'s one-landing gate, `engine`'s alarm-reading producer gate, `queue/jetstream/brokertest`'s raw-server gate and `code`'s read gate (a `*sql.Tx`'s, `*sql.DB`'s or `*sql.Conn`'s `ExecContext` takes a statement's text where a `*sql.Stmt`'s takes its arguments: one name, told apart by the declaration) — read from source with no type checker, because a type checker types every package the judged ones import (41 s cold for `cmd/crewlet`). THREE ANSWERS, NEVER TWO: a `Type` is known, `Unread` (only a package it does not read could type it, and that package is named) or unknown, and a `Selection` is a field or a method with the declared type that holds it, `Beyond` (a part it does not read may hold it), `FromUnread` (the receiver is itself a value only a package it does not read could type), `Absent` or `Undetermined` — a member found DEEPER than a part it could not read included, since that part may shadow it — and what each answer MEANS is the gate's: the stream-identity gate reports an unread value, the pacing gate, which reads `net/http`, passes one. `ImportName` is the one rule for an unnamed import's name (a major version, a gopkg.in `.vN`, `.go`, `go-`), which the rendezvous and gitproc gates read too. Lifted when the second gate's private walker had already drifted from the first's — one could not name `nats.go`, the other `yaml.v3`, and only one followed generics (ADR-0008); a normal package rather than a test file because eight gates' tests read it |
| `conflictmarkers` | A test-only package — what it certifies is content rather than code, as `internal/docslinks` does for the docs' links — that FAILS THE BUILD on a file in this tree still carrying a merge conflict's markers. A Go file with one fails to compile, the one place a marker is loud; everywhere else it is silent — a docs page renders it as prose and the site publishes it, a YAML or SQL comment swallows it, the committed dashboard bundle ships it — and a long branch resolves the same page one commit at a time, each commit permanent history. | `adr` | The gate behind `adr/`: every record carries its fields under a number no other record holds, names an Authority that exists and mentions it, and an Enforced-by gate that exists, in the package a name qualified by one says (or the literal `nothing`, saying why); every citation of a record names one that exists, and the index names every record. It runs inside `make check` because the register it replaced, `docs/reference/design-decisions.md`, was referred to by nothing and drifted until it described an engine that no longer existed |
| `version` | What the binary calls itself: the tag goreleaser stamps at link time (for the image of `main`, `main-` and twelve hex digits of the commit, stamped the same way), falling back to the module's own build info and then to `dev`, so a binary built outside the release path names itself honestly rather than claiming to be a release it is not. `IsDevelopment` is the one PREDICATE over that, and it is an ALLOWLIST of the two unversioned spellings (`dev`, `(devel)`) rather than a test for a release shape — its caller is the development principal, which authenticates every request with no credential, so a spelling this build does not recognise, `main-<commit>` among them, must refuse the bypass rather than enable it. They used to be ten times its code and to assert the RELEASE SURFACE instead — the ldflags stamp, the pure-Go build, the image's `${TARGETPLATFORM}` copy, the catch-all notes category, the pre-release flags, the single tag trigger and every Dependabot entry — because each of those fails silently and has no other symptom |
| `testbinary` | WHETHER THIS PROCESS IS A TEST BINARY, for the few rules shipping code holds only a test to — a broker and Gitlet in a test declare their sizes (`jetstream.ErrUndeclaredSize`, `engine.ErrUndeclaredCodeCache`).
